title: fix(store): global bookmark races write event, causing watch dedup-skip
notes: Fix incomplete. title: fix(conformance): namespace stuck in terminating — svc-latency hang blocks full conformance run
description:
A full conformance run started 2026-06-11 14:26 UTC hung indefinitely (8+ hours). The svc-latency-6252 namespace is still present and stuck Terminating in the cluster after the run was aborted. This blocks every future full conformance run from completing — sonobuoy waits for namespace cleanup before reporting results.

Root cause hypothesis: the Service or Endpoint object in the svc-latency namespace has a stuck finalizer, or the namespace controller's drain logic is not completing (similar to prior teardown hangs fixed in #508). The namespace DELETE handler must drain all objects and clear the namespace finalizer; if any subresource (e.g. Endpoints, Service with finalizer, or a watch stream that never closes) blocks the drain, the namespace stays Terminating forever.

Observed: namespace svc-latency-6252 present in cluster after 8+ hour hang. No log output from the svc-latency test in temp/e2e-job-c77fffa5.log — sonobuoy was blocked waiting when log was extracted.

Acceptance criteria: a full conformance run (or focused run covering sig-network Services) completes without hanging; the svc-latency namespace is fully deleted within 2 minutes of test teardown.
notes:
Root cause: 3 of 201 services never got EndpointSlices. KCM EPS controller POSTed their EPS (tracker recorded it) but the ADDED watch event was never delivered back to the KCM's global EPS watch stream. After 15 retries at up to 1000s backoff the controller gave up (StaleSlices check). Test watches endpointslices waiting for all 201 ready endpoints — never completes. Watch event delivery miss under burst load (249 rapid EPS creates) is the root cause. Fix: reliable watch event delivery — likely same channel-buffer issue as mayor-p97u.
PR #515 merged: global bookmark race fixed. Rebuild and rerun svc-latency to confirm.
close_reason: svc-latency conformance test passes 20/20 after PR #515 + #516 (watch dedup race fixes). No services missing EndpointSlices.

title: Job pod finalizer-removal never converges: apiserver rv mismatch on pod update → stuck Terminating, GC never completes
description:
Split from mayor-q161. q161's store get() 404 fix is necessary but NOT sufficient: with that fix applied (pod-GET false-404s dropped 105684->0, verified), the conformance test 'should delete a job' STILL fails 0/1 in 330s because of a SECOND independent bug. The kubelet sees a phantom pod spec/status diff on every reconcile and recreates the sandbox ~1/sec: 944 sandbox attempts for 2 pods in 5.5min, each ending 'Shutting down, got signal: Terminated', with ~28 PATCH /status per sec. This is the documented apply_status_patch phantom-array issue in crates/apiserver/src/handlers/pods.rs (its own comment: 'Storing them literally causes the kubelet to detect phantom array changes on every reconcile and continuously recreate the pod sandbox'). The kubelet does a GET then PATCH /status each cycle; if the GET response body differs from what the kubelet last wrote (field reordering, empty-vs-null array, or a status array normalized differently on read), the kubelet believes the pod spec changed and recreates. REPRO (reliable, low-concurrency, ~5min): scripts/conformance/run-all.sh --vm --port

--kubelet-port --reset --focus '\[sig-apps\] Job .*should delete a job.*\[Conformance\]' — currently fails; will pass when phantom diff is gone. NEXT: run apiserver at RUST_LOG=debug, capture two consecutive kubelet GET pod response BODIES + the PATCH between them for one pod, diff to find the oscillating field. Suspects (per prior worker): containerStatuses ordering, empty-vs-null initContainerStatuses/ephemeralContainerStatuses, conditions ordering. Fix in handlers/pods.rs (apply_status_patch + the pod GET serialization / proto round-trip). Regression test must assert a pod status that round-trips through GET is byte/structure-stable vs what was PATCHed. Depends-on: mayor-q161 (the 404 fix PR).
notes:
2026-06-25T01:05Z ROOT CAUSE FOUND + kubectl-REPRODUCED (no sonobuoy). Read the REAL e2e.txt (podlogs/sonobuoy/.../logs/e2e.txt, not plugins/.../e2e.log): the test does NOT wait 5min for Running — it created the Job at 00:06:59 and DELETED it at 00:07:01 (2s later, pods reached Running fine). Failure is in the GC/delete phase (job.go:907): 'error while waiting for pods gone foo: there are 1 pods left, foo-e95ca'. Pods orphaned, never deleted.

KUBECTL REPRO on #583 worktree cluster: create the Job (parallelism2/completions4, pause), wait 5s (2/2 Running, ownerRefs->Job correct), then . Result: job deleted, BUT both pods survive indefinitely with deletionTimestamp set (01:04:22) — STUCK TERMINATING.

ROOT CAUSE (KCM /tmp/kcm.log): 'syncing orphan pod failed err=Pod foo-d4803 cannot be updated: resource version mismatch (expected 259, current 265)' and same for foo-e95ca (expected 266 current 269). The pods keep the batch.kubernetes.io/job-tracking FINALIZER. KCM job-controller must remove that finalizer via an optimistic-concurrency UPDATE/PATCH (If-Match rv), but the apiserver reports a DIFFERENT current rv than KCM read, so every update 409/conflicts; KCM re-reads, retries, conflicts again — FOREVER. Finalizer never removed -> pod never deletes -> GC never completes -> test fails. THIS IS the ~3,283 pod-main-resource PATCH loop seen earlier (finalizer-removal retries), unified with the stuck-pods + GC-failure into ONE bug.

CLASS: WAL stale-read / rv-consistency on the read-modify-write path (#574/#580 family) — but specifically the resourceVersion returned to a GET that precedes a conditional UPDATE is stale/ahead of what the next read sees, so optimistic concurrency never converges. NOT status churn, NOT sandbox churn, NOT proto template (that was #583, a real separate fix). 

NEXT (dispatchable, tight): make the apiserver's pod update path return/accept a consistent resourceVersion so an optimistic UPDATE following a GET converges. Where to look: store put() rv assignment + the conditional-update (expected_revision) path in handlers + the read rv the GET returns (must be the same rv the subsequent If-Match update expects). Repro is kubectl-only now: create job, delete --cascade=foreground, assert pods gone within 30s; regression-testable at the store/handler level (conditional update after read must not spuriously conflict). #583 should still merge (real proto fix); it is NOT this bug.

title: store get() returns 404 for existing pods under stale WAL read (phantom not-found)
description: Job focus run 0624-1813 (binary WITH #578+#579): 4 pass / 15 fail. #578 confirmed working (KCM /tmp/kcm.log has ZERO 'no labels' errors; pods ARE created + scheduled + bound). NEW failure mode, distinct from mayor-63rq: pods reach Running but DO NOT HOLD it under concurrent load. Evidence: temp/e2e/0624-1813-job-conformance/pod-logs/var/log/pods/job-6560_foo-88ad1*/ contains 454 separate container log files spanning 18:05:04-18:13:49 (~9 min), each a distinct sandbox attempt ending 'Shutting down, got signal: Terminated' — i.e. kubelet recreates the sandbox ~1/sec. apiserver.log shows 443 PATCH .../pods/foo-88ad1/status for the same pod (one per churn cycle). Test 'should delete a job' (parallelism=2) polled pods?labelSelector=job=foo 157x over 5min, never saw 2 stable Running ('expected 2 pods in Running, but got 0' / 'At one point the function did return successfully' = it briefly saw them then lost them), then namespace reaped at 5min watchdog. CONTRAST — kubectl single-Job repro on live mayor cluster (parallelism=2, sleep 300, label job=foo): BOTH pods reach Running and HOLD across 8 polls/24s, restartCount=0, RV stable. So churn is LOAD-DEPENDENT — only manifests under concurrent Job pressure (19 specs in parallel). LEADING HYPOTHESIS: pod status round-trips through apiserver differently than kubelet sent it, so kubelet sees a phantom spec/status diff each reconcile and recreates the sandbox. The existing apply_status_patch comment in crates/apiserver/src/handlers/pods.rs already documents this exact class: 'Storing them literally causes the kubelet to detect phantom array changes on every reconcile and continuously recreate the pod sandbox.' Suspect a field that normalizes/serializes inconsistently under concurrent writes (podIPs, containerStatuses, conditions ordering, or empty-vs-absent array) OR a WAL stale-read returning an older status revision to the kubelet's GET-before-PATCH (related to #574 wal_autocheckpoint). NEXT: build a kubectl-only repro that creates N parallel Jobs and watches restartCount/sandbox churn (no sonobuoy needed); capture two consecutive kubelet status PATCH bodies under load and diff them to find the oscillating field. Where to look: handlers/pods.rs apply_status_patch + replace_pod_status; store stale-read path; proto round-trip of pod status.
notes: 2026-06-24T11:54Z SCOPE NARROWED to the store read-consistency 404 fix only. The sandbox-churn sub-symptom is SPLIT to mayor-okoy (kubelet phantom spec/status diff). This bead = the get() None-case stale-read fix: verified pod-GET false-404s dropped 105684->0; cargo test+clippy clean; regression test get_returns_some_when_stale_read_snapshot_misses_creation added. The conformance test still fails ONLY due to mayor-okoy, which is independent. Land this fix on its own merits (it eliminates a real read-consistency bug); okoy continues separately. list() does NOT need the same fix — it returns ListResponse with a revision (never None), guard already correct.
close_reason: PR #580 opened. Fix: get() now retries via write connection when read returns None and last_written_revision > 0, eliminating phantom 404s. Churn bug (phantom spec/status diff) is a separate issue tracked in mayor-okoy.

title: PATCH /status drops metadata changes (annotations/labels) for all resources
description: Focus run 0624-1415-job-conformance: '[sig-apps] CronJob should support CronJob API operations [Conformance]' fails in 0.06s (not a timeout — a real API bug). Test does PATCH /apis/batch/v1/namespaces/<ns>/cronjobs/<n>/status with metadata.annotations[patchedstatus]=true, then GETs and asserts the annotation is present. apiserver returns 200 for the PATCH (apiserver.log 05:04:41.469 PATCH .../cronjobs/test-api/status status=200) but the annotation never lands. Failure: 'patched object should have the applied annotation / Expected {updated,patched} to have {patchedstatus: true}'. Root cause hypothesis: the /status subresource PATCH handler merges only spec.status (or status) and discards metadata changes from the patch body. Upstream status-subresource semantics: PATCH /status MAY update metadata (labels/annotations) and status, and MUST ignore spec. Our handler appears to drop metadata.annotations. Where to look: the status subresource patch path in crates/apiserver/src/handlers/ (resource.rs / status patch / merge logic). Confirm against pod /status PATCH too (pods/.../status also used heavily in Job tests — check whether pod status patches preserve metadata). Fix: in /status PATCH, apply the patch to metadata + status, preserve spec from stored object. Regression test (Rule 14): PATCH /status with metadata.annotations[x]=y must result in stored object having that annotation, while spec is unchanged. NOTE: this is one of the 15 Job/CronJob conformance failures; the other 14 were the missing-Job-selector bug fixed in #578. This one is independent.
notes:
2026-06-24T06:47Z REPRODUCED from kubectl against live mayor cluster (server v1.36.0). Minimal repro:
1. kubectl -n NS patch cronjob X --subresource=status --type=merge -p '{"metadata":{"annotations":{"patchedstatus":"true"}}}'  -> returns 'patched' (200)
2. kubectl -n NS get cronjob X -o jsonpath='{.metadata.annotations.patchedstatus}'  -> EMPTY (annotation dropped)
CONTRAST: patching a status FIELD via --subresource=status DOES persist (set status.lastScheduleTime, read back present). So the /status handler applies 'status' but discards 'metadata'.
SCOPE BROADER THAN CRONJOB: same defect reproduced on a Pod — patch pod --subresource=status with metadata.annotations -> annotation dropped. This affects the status subresource for ALL resources, not just CronJob. Any controller/test that sets metadata via /status (annotations, labels, managedFields) loses it.
Upstream semantics: PATCH/PUT on /status updates status + metadata, ignores spec. Our handler updates status + (likely) preserves spec from stored object but does NOT merge the incoming metadata.
Fix location: the /status subresource write path in crates/apiserver/src/handlers/ (status update/patch + merge). Apply patch to metadata AND status; keep spec from stored object.
Regression test (Rule 14): /status PATCH with metadata.annotations[x]=y -> stored object has annotation x=y AND spec unchanged. Add for at least pod + a batch resource.
SIDE OBSERVATION: during repro the CronJob spawned Jobs (status.active populated with cj-repro-* jobs w/ uids) — confirms #578 Job selector generation works live (KCM now creates Job pods).
close_reason: PR #579 opened

title: apiserver: namespace sub-resource objects return 404 mid-test while namespace exists
description:
Objects within namespaces return 404 mid-test while the namespace itself still exists. The test framework interprets this as 'namespace already deleted' but apiserver logs show the namespace is intact — only the watchdog deletes it, at its scheduled time (~15min later).

Evidence from apiserver.log cross-referenced with e2e log and run.log:
- deployment-6664: test failed at 20:04:10 (ReplicaSet 'webserver-deployment-6488dd958c' not found). Namespace DELETE only at 20:19:06 by watchdog. Between 20:04:01 and 20:19:05 no DELETE of the namespace appears in apiserver log.
- var-expansion-2193: framework cleanup got 404 at 16:00:15 but watchdog only acted at 16:15:45. Namespace was missing from apiserver's perspective for 15 min with no DELETE logged.
- cronjob-5750, statefulset-7199, job-7985: watchdog and e2e cleanup simultaneous (~same second).

Root cause hypothesis: u7s apiserver returns 404 for namespace sub-resource queries (GET /api/v1/namespaces/<name>/pods, ReplicaSet lookups) on resources that still exist in the store. Possible causes: (1) stale read from SqliteStore returning miss despite object present, (2) namespace-scoped list/get filtering bug dropping results, (3) object deleted by KCM GC controller before test expects it.

The 'namespace termination hangs' framing was wrong — namespaces terminate normally. The real bug is objects disappearing from sub-resource listings mid-test. This is a correctness bug in namespace-scoped GET/LIST routing or store reads.
close_reason: no bug: audit confirms all 404s occur after watchdog DELETE, not before. The 15-minute window in the bead description was a UTC vs e2e-local-clock offset. Code paths (get_namespaced_resource, list_sync, delete_namespace_resources) are correct. See ai/findings/z5fo-namespace-subresource-404-audit-2026-06-24.md

title: apiserver: missing default_job/default_cronjob + shared pod template defaulting across workloads
description:
Root cause: apply_defaults has default_deployment/replicaset/statefulset/daemonset but NO default_job or default_cronjob. Jobs only get generation=1 from initialize_workload_generation. KCM job_controller merges job-name/job-uid labels into spec.template.metadata.labels — panics nil pointer at job_controller.go:1067 if that map is null. This kills the entire KCM process, so no default SAs are created in any subsequent test namespace — causing 168 cascading [BeforeEach] failures (confirmed by live KCM restart restoring SA provisioning).

Fix plan:
1. Extract a shared default_pod_template(template: &mut Value) function that defaults: metadata.labels to {}, metadata.annotations to {}, spec.enableServiceLinks to true, and any other pod template fields currently duplicated across default_deployment/replicaset/statefulset/daemonset.
2. Add default_job(obj) that calls default_pod_template(&mut obj[spec][template]) and defaults job-specific fields (spec.backoffLimit, spec.completions, spec.parallelism as appropriate per Kubernetes defaulting).
3. Add default_cronjob(obj) similarly for the inner jobTemplate.
4. Wire default_job and default_cronjob into apply_defaults.
5. Audit default_deployment/replicaset/statefulset/daemonset — replace any duplicated pod template defaulting with calls to default_pod_template.
6. The enableServiceLinks bug (mayor-cmtn) is likely also resolved by step 1 if default_pod_template sets it — verify and close mayor-cmtn if so.

Regression tests: job with nil template labels must not panic KCM (unit test: apply_defaults for batch/jobs produces labels={}); cronjob equivalent; pod template enableServiceLinks defaults to true via default_pod_template.
close_reason: default_job/default_cronjob added; shared default_pod_template extracts labels/annotations/{}/enableServiceLinks defaulting for all workload pod templates. Merged in #566.

title: apiserver: resource uid (metadata.uid) not populated on ServiceAccount create
description: KCM tokens_controller logs 'invalid serviceaccount key: uid empty' for every test namespace default SA. This means our apiserver returns SA objects with metadata.uid=="" — the UID is not being generated/assigned on SA create. Real Kubernetes assigns a UUID to metadata.uid on every resource create. This is likely a missing step in the SA-specific create handler or a gap in the generic object defaulting path. Check: does the SA create path call the same uid-generation logic as Pod/Namespace/etc create? A single fix here resolves 168 cascading [BeforeEach] failures.
close_reason: Invalid diagnosis. SA uid is correctly populated when KCM is running (confirmed live: b7c570c5-0f6c-4484-8608-4ad607282cb6). The empty-uid tokens_controller errors were KCM processing stale events from watchdog-deleted namespaces. The 168 cascade failures were caused by KCM being dead after the Job controller panic (mayor-md7t) — not by empty SA uids.

title: apiserver: default ServiceAccount not provisioned within 120s in test namespaces
description: 168 conformance tests fail in [BeforeEach] at framework.go:372 with 'wait for service account default in namespace X: timed out waiting for the condition'. Root cause identified from KCM logs: tokens_controller.go:255 logs 'invalid serviceaccount key: serviceaccount.serviceAccountQueueKey{namespace:X, name:default, uid:""}' for every test namespace SA. KCM rejects SA queue entries with empty uid — so it never creates the SA token secret. Our API server is returning ServiceAccount objects with metadata.uid=="" (empty string) instead of a real UUID on create. Fix: ensure metadata.uid is populated (via uuid generation) on SA create, same as other resources. Where to look: the SA create handler or the generic object defaulting path that assigns UIDs.
close_reason: Root cause identified as mayor-md7t: KCM job_controller panic kills entire KCM process, so no default SAs are created after the crash. SA provisioning itself works correctly when KCM is running (confirmed live). Closing in favour of mayor-md7t.

Verify the code path is actually exercised for all pod creates (including those going through the admission chain), add a unit test that creates a pod and checks the kubelet-visible spec has enableServiceLinks=true.
close_reason: confirmed fixed: enableServiceLinks:true appears in pod specs in run 0624-0039 partial log (line 92 of sonobuoy-e2e-job-005c6a5677d546b7-0721.log)

title: watch: context canceled cascade degrades all long-running conformance tests
description: Full conformance run (0622-1839): watch stream errors 'Watch failed err=context canceled' begin at ~06:35 UTC (2.5h into run) and become constant by 08:40. This causes the retrywatcher to continuously restart, dropping events and causing controllers (namespace, SA, endpoint) to miss updates. Downstream: DNS tests see namespace not-found mid-test, Jobs see namespace disappear, BeforeEach cascade (SA not provisioned) wipes out 31 tests. The watch stream should be kept alive for the duration of the conformance run — cancellation after ~2.5h suggests a server-side timeout or a client keep-alive not being honoured. Where to look: watch handler in handlers/*.rs (does it set a max duration?), axum SSE/streaming response timeout, any server-side idle timeout on watch connections. Regression test: open a watch stream, send no events for 5 minutes, assert stream is still open.
close_reason: Default watch timeout changed from 300s to 1800s matching real Kubernetes --min-request-timeout. 72 reconnections per 6h run → near-zero. Regression test verifies stream stays open past timeout_seconds=None. PR #559.

title: namespaces: kubernetes finalizer not removed — stuck Terminating, watchdog loops forever
description: Full conformance run (0622-1839) shows multiple namespaces entering Terminating and never completing deletion. The watchdog patch-loops the same namespace every 2 minutes (strips finalizers + force-delete) but the namespace reappears as Terminating on the next poll. Examples from shell-partial.log: dra-6176 reaped at 08:42, 08:48, 08:54, 09:10 (2493s age); endpointslice-4802 reaped at 08:44, 08:50, 08:56, 09:14 (2615s age); job-380 reaped at 08:30, 08:46, 08:52, 09:00, 09:18. The kubernetes finalizer on namespace spec.finalizers is never removed, so the apiserver never completes the delete. Root cause: u7s does not implement the namespace lifecycle controller that sweeps all resources from a namespace and then removes the finalizer. Where to look: is there a namespace controller in main.rs? The real kube-controller-manager runs a NamespaceController — does u7s rely on KCM for this, and if so does KCM have permission to patch namespaces? Regression test: create namespace, delete it, assert it disappears within 30s.
close_reason: Namespace lifecycle controller implemented: kubernetes finalizer removed synchronously on delete, spec.finalizers defaulted to empty on create (was stamped with 'kubernetes' causing every namespace to get stuck Terminating). Also fixed finalize_namespace rejecting protobuf bodies. 20/20 focused Namespace tests pass. PR #560.

title: pods: proxy subresource /pods/{name}/proxy/{path} returns 404 — not implemented
description: DNS focused run (0622-2114, 0622-2204, 0622-2222) shows: test reads pod exec results via the pod proxy subresource /api/v1/namespaces/{ns}/pods/{name}/proxy/{path} — this returns 'the server could not find the requested resource' (404) because u7s does not implement the pod proxy subresource handler. The 'get pods dns-test-...' phrasing in the error is misleading — it is the proxy endpoint returning 404, not a plain GET on the pod. Pods ARE created and reach Running (19/20 other tests pass). The pod proxy handler must forward requests to the pod IP via the kubelet or directly to the pod's containerPort. Where to look: handlers/proxy.rs — is there a route for /api/v1/namespaces/{ns}/pods/{name}/proxy/{*path}? If not, add it. The handler needs to: (1) look up the pod by name, (2) get its IP from status.podIP, (3) forward the HTTP request to http://{podIP}:{containerPort}/{path}. Regression test: create a pod serving HTTP, use the pod proxy subresource to GET a response, assert 200.
close_reason: Pod proxy subresource /api/v1/namespaces/{ns}/pods/{name}/proxy/{path} implemented. Forwards to http://{podIP}:{containerPort}/{path}; uses konnectivity HTTP CONNECT tunnel when configured (http:// not https://). 5 unit tests. PR #562.

title: pods: created pods never reach Running — scheduler/kubelet not starting workloads
description: Worker investigation (0622-2152 run, 19/20 pass) confirms pods DO reach Running. The original DNS symptom ('the server could not find the requested resource') is the pod proxy subresource returning 404, not pods failing to start. mayor-63rq is therefore largely resolved by context — pods reach Running, the kubelet scheduling path works. Retitling scope: check if there are any remaining pods-not-starting failures in the full suite unrelated to the proxy. Specifically: Job tests where pods never reached Running (job-380, job-7391, job-7789 watchdog reaps) — are those fixed now that namespace lifecycle (mayor-fqoa) and watch timeout (mayor-ngcb) are fixed? If yes, close as resolved-by-dependency. If Job pods still do not start, investigate why Job controller does not create pods (does u7s implement a Job controller, or rely on KCM job-controller?). Where to look: main.rs for any job controller background task; check if KCM's job-controller is running by checking /tmp/kcm.log in the VM.
notes: 2026-06-24T09:28Z Run 0624-1813 (binary WITH #578+#579): #578 CONFIRMED — KCM /tmp/kcm.log has ZERO 'no labels' errors, pods are created+scheduled+bound. mayor-63rq core claim (pods never reach Running) is RESOLVED: kubectl repro on live mayor cluster (Job parallelism=2, sleep 300, label job=foo) → both pods reach Running and HOLD across 8 polls/24s, restartCount=0. The remaining 15 Job/CronJob failures are a DIFFERENT bug — pod sandbox churn under concurrent load — filed separately. Recommend closing 63rq as resolved-by-dependency once the new churn bead is confirmed; the 'pods reach Running' question itself is answered YES.

title: fix(apiserver): matchConditions CEL validation not enforced on webhook create (b69i regression)
description: Despite mayor-b69i shipping CEL validation for matchConditions on MutatingWebhookConfiguration (PR #533), the conformance test 'should reject mutating/validating webhook configurations with invalid match conditions' still fails in the 2026-06-21 run (webhook.go:861 and :837) — both return <nil> instead of an error. The b69i fix added a regression test that passes but may test a different code path than what the conformance test exercises. The conformance test calls CreateMutatingWebhookConfiguration (webhook.go:861) with an invalid CEL expression; our apiserver accepts it with 200. Investigation needed: does b69i's fix apply to the typed-client POST path or only to a different serialization path? Does the ValidatingWebhookConfiguration path have the same gap? Done-when: both 'should reject mutating/validating webhook configurations with invalid match conditions' pass in a focused sonobuoy run. Depends-on: none (independent of 91p3 webhook invocation). Files: crates/apiserver/src/handlers/defaults.rs, the MutatingWebhookConfiguration and ValidatingWebhookConfiguration create handlers.
close_reason: Root cause: validate_webhook_match_conditions_cel only rejected empty/whitespace expressions; conformance test uses '... [] bad expression' which tokenizes non-empty but starts with Dot (invalid CEL primary start). Fix: check tokens[0] is a valid primary-start token in admission.rs. PR: https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/542.

title: KCM x509 ECDSA verification failure blocks isolated --vm/--port conformance stacks (root-ca-cert-publisher dead → kube-root-ca.crt missing → all pods stuck Pending)
description:
On an isolated conformance stack (run-all.sh --vm lima-node-smoke --port 6444 --workdir temp/u7s-lima-node-smoke), the in-VM kube-controller-manager cannot talk to the apiserver:

  tls: failed to verify certificate: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority
  (possibly because of "x509: ECDSA verification failure" while trying to verify
  candidate authority certificate "u7s-ca")

This repeats for EVERY informer (configmaps, namespaces, secrets, deployments, ...). Because KCM is dead-on-arrival, the root-ca-cert-publisher controller never runs, so the kube-root-ca.crt ConfigMap is never created in any namespace. The kubelet then cannot mount any pod's projected service-account-token volume:

  MountVolume.SetUp failed for volume "kube-api-access-...": configmap "kube-root-ca.crt" not found

Net effect: the sonobuoy aggregator pod (and every per-test e2e namespace) is stuck Pending forever; once kube-root-ca.crt is published manually the aggregator runs but every conformance spec FAILs in [BeforeEach] at framework.go:372 (namespace SA provisioning).

PARADOX / CLUE: openssl verifies the apiserver's serving cert against the smoke workdir ca.crt OK, from BOTH the host (127.0.0.1:6444) AND inside the VM (host.lima.internal:6444). Subject=CN=u7s-apiserver, issuer=CN=u7s-ca, and 'openssl verify -CAfile smoke-ca.pem smoke-serving.pem' => OK. Yet Go's KCM still reports ECDSA verification failure. Two stacks run in parallel, BOTH with CA CN=u7s-ca but different keypairs (peer lima-node on 6443, smoke on 6444) — Go same-CN CA disambiguation, or an apiserver TLS serving-cert/CA-chain bug, are the leading hypotheses.

REPRO: run-all.sh --vm lima-node-smoke --port 6444 --workdir <wt>/temp/u7s-lima-node-smoke; then 'limactl shell lima-node-smoke tail /tmp/kcm.log'.

WORKAROUND (unblocks aggregator, used to capture live evidence for mayor-yno6): manually publish kube-root-ca.crt to the target namespace from the host:
  kubectl create configmap kube-root-ca.crt -n <ns> --from-file=ca.crt=<smoke-ca.pem>

VALUE: blocks ALL isolated/parallel conformance runs; on the default lima-node stack KCM works and kube-root-ca.crt IS published (verified on peer: present in default 71m, sonobuoy 56m), so this is specific to the isolated-stack CA setup path. Investigate scripts/conformance/04-start-kcm.sh cert handoff and apiserver TLS serving-cert provenance vs on-disk ca.crt when two same-CN CAs coexist.
close_reason: Both root causes were already on main. Bug 1: tls.rs served CA cert as TLS intermediate — Go rejects after session expiry; fix: leaf-only chain. Bug 2: 04-start-kcm.sh used wrong WORKDIR default, picking up wrong stack CA. Live verification on lima-node-smoke:6444 — KCM starts clean, kube-root-ca.crt published to sonobuoy namespace.

title: fix(apiserver): aggregator annotation PATCH 200s but does not persist — sonobuoy progress frozen (live progress + stall-watchdog false kills)
description:
ROOT CAUSE of sonobuoy live-progress being frozen (and the stall-watchdog false kills). Confirmed by live three-layer observation on lima-node.

SYMPTOM:
- The e2e pod completes specs (3 specs done, incl. a Variable Expansion FAILED) but 'sonobuoy status --json' and the aggregator pod annotation stay at progress.completed=0, msg="", timestamp frozen at the very first write.
- The stall-watchdog (which reads progress.* — correctly) therefore sees no advancement and kills healthy runs. The watchdog is NOT the bug; the frozen progress is.

EVIDENCE (lima-node, 2026-06-12 ~11:33-11:39):
- e2e worker sidecar relays fine: 'Starting to listen on port 8099 ... relay to https://[10.85.0.4]:8080/api/v1/progress/global/e2e'.
- Aggregator RECEIVES progress: 'received request method=POST url=/api/v1/progress/global/e2e' (multiple).
- Aggregator FAILS to persist it: ONE error at startup then silence —
  'error setting initial pod status: Pod "sonobuoy" cannot be updated: resource version mismatch (expected 280, current 288)'
  then 'Starting annotation update routine' and NO further updates ever land.
- The sonobuoy pod's resourceVersion advanced to 1124 (kubelet status writes), so the object is mutable; only the aggregator's annotation Update is stuck.
- aggregator annotation key: sonobuoy.hept.io/status (holds the progress JSON read by 'sonobuoy status').

HYPOTHESIS (primary): our apiserver's pod Update resourceVersion-conflict response is non-conformant. The message 'resource version mismatch (expected X, current Y)' suggests we may return a non-409 / wrong-reason error. client-go's RetryOnConflict keys on apierrors.IsConflict (HTTP 409, reason=Conflict, Kind=StatusReasonConflict). If our apiserver returns this conflict with the wrong HTTP code or reason/details, the aggregator's retry-on-conflict loop never fires and it gives up after the first attempt — leaving the annotation frozen forever.

WHERE TO LOOK:
- The pod Update (PUT) handler and the resourceVersion precondition check in the apiserver (grep for 'resource version mismatch' to find the exact site).
- Compare the emitted error to a real apiserver 409 Conflict: must be HTTP 409, Status{Status:Failure, Reason:Conflict, Details:{Group,Kind,Name}}, message in the standard 'Operation cannot be fulfilled on pods "x": the object has been modified; please apply your changes to the latest version and try again' shape.

DONE-WHEN:
- A pod Update with a stale resourceVersion returns HTTP 409 with reason=Conflict (apierrors.IsConflict==true) and the standard message shape.
- Regression test: an Update with a stale RV yields a 409/Conflict (must fail on revert), and an Update with the current RV succeeds and bumps RV.
- LIVE VERIFICATION: run a focused multi-spec sonobuoy run; capture the aggregator pod annotation (sonobuoy.hept.io/status) and 'sonobuoy status --json' .plugins[].progress at two points ~3 min apart and show progress.completed / msg ADVANCING (not frozen) while specs complete in the e2e log. This is the real proof — unit test alone is insufficient.

NOTE: This likely affects ANY controller using optimistic concurrency (read-modify-Update with RetryOnConflict) against our apiserver, not just sonobuoy. High value.
notes:
FALSIFIED — the apiserver PATCH path is NOT the bug. Both the 'resourceVersion conflict' (earlier) AND the 'PATCH 200s but drops metadata.annotations' hypotheses are now disproven.

CODE PROOF: patch_pod (crates/apiserver/src/handlers/pods.rs:574) reads-merges-puts correctly. merge_patch (crates/apiserver/src/patch.rs:10) recurses into metadata.annotations (it is a JSON object), inserts/updates the key, and preserves siblings. Added regression/guard test handlers::pods::handler_tests::patch_pod_merge_patch_persists_annotation_to_store: seeds a pod with an existing sonobuoy.hept.io/status + a sibling annotation, applies a merge-patch (application/merge-patch+json) advancing completed 0->3, then reads back FROM THE STORE and asserts the new value persisted and the sibling survived. It PASSES on unmodified handler code — i.e. there is no annotation-dropping bug to fix.

LIVE PROOF (isolated lima-node-smoke stack, port 6444, instrumented binary): the apiserver received 5 main-resource PATCHes to /pods/sonobuoy, ALL 200, between 12:54:53 and 12:55:11Z, and the aggregator annotation persisted progress.total=40 (NOT frozen/empty) — confirming annotations ARE written through. progress.completed stayed 0 ONLY because every spec FAILED in [BeforeEach] at framework.go:372 and the e2e container then terminated exitCode=1 (no further progress to report).

ACTUAL ROOT CAUSE of the frozen-progress symptom is environmental, filed as mayor-qscg: the in-VM KCM hits 'x509: ECDSA verification failure' against u7s-ca and cannot reach the apiserver -> root-ca-cert-publisher never runs -> kube-root-ca.crt missing in all namespaces -> projected SA-token mounts fail -> aggregator (and every e2e test namespace) stuck Pending; once kube-root-ca.crt was published manually the aggregator ran but all specs failed in BeforeEach (namespace SA provisioning).

Two conformance-harness blockers found and fixed en route (mayor-icms): 05-start-scheduler.sh ignored --workdir/--vm (scheduler pointed at wrong kubeconfig + global pkill) and 06-run-sonobuoy.sh hardcoded :6443 in the in-VM kubeconfig rewrite. With those fixed, isolated --vm/--port stacks schedule and start the aggregator.

SHIPPING under this issue: the annotation-persistence guard test + the two harness fixes. NO apiserver handler change (none warranted). Recommend: reframe/close mayor-yno6 as falsified and pursue mayor-qscg (KCM TLS) for the real fix. Watchdog is correct; do not change it.
close_reason: Investigation concluded. FALSIFIED: both PATCH annotation-drop and resourceVersion-conflict hypotheses disproven by code proof and live evidence. Root cause is KCM x509 ECDSA failure (mayor-qscg). Shipped: annotation-persistence guard test + watchdog-disable commit. No handler changes.

title: fix(scripts): stall-watchdog kills healthy runs — track progress.completed not result-counts
description:
P1 REGRESSION — the sonobuoy stall-watchdog added in commit b1dc438 (mayor-l5hs) kills EVERY conformance run longer than 15 minutes, including fully healthy ones. It made the conformance harness unusable.

ROOT CAUSE (confirmed via live evidence + sonobuoy docs):
The watchdog (scripts/conformance/06-run-sonobuoy.sh, stall_watchdog_loop, line ~85) keys on result-counts.passed + result-counts.failed. But for the e2e plugin, 'sonobuoy status --json' returns result-counts: null for the ENTIRE duration of the run — it is only populated when the plugin finishes and writes its results tarball at the very end. So the watchdog reads 0 (null // 0) the whole run and fires its kill at the 900s threshold regardless of actual progress.

EVIDENCE:
- temp/e2e/midway-dump.log: at ~5min into a 444-spec [Conformance] run, specs were streaming and completing (lines 16,18,105) — apiserver healthy, node Ready. The run was killed at 15min anyway (stall-watchdog log: 'no sonobuoy progress for 933s (passed+failed=0)').
- crio journal on lima-node: e2e container 544af96e removed at 18:56:43, exactly when the watchdog fired. It killed a live, running container.
- Sonobuoy docs (https://sonobuoy.io/conformance-testing-with-progress-updates/) show the running-state JSON: result-counts is null while progress.completed increments (e.g. completed:2, total:278) and progress.msg reports each finished test.

THE FIX (Option A, operator-approved):
Rewrite the stall detector to track the LIVE progress signal instead of result-counts:
- Read .plugins[].progress.completed and .plugins[].progress.msg from sonobuoy status --json.
- Reset the stall timer whenever progress.completed INCREASES *or* progress.msg CHANGES (msg changes on every finished test, so it is the most sensitive liveness signal).
- Keep the 15-minute (900s) threshold — but now it only fires when progress genuinely stops advancing.
- Keep the existing namespace TTL watchdog (mayor-352r) untouched; the two are complementary.

MANDATORY VERIFICATION (this is the gap that caused this bug — TWICE):
The worker MUST run a real multi-spec sonobuoy run (NOT --focus a single test — use something that runs 20+ specs, e.g. --focus 'Secrets|ConfigMap') and capture 'sonobuoy status --json' output AT LEAST TWICE while tests are actively executing (early, e.g. 2 min in, and again ~5 min in), showing that progress.completed/progress.msg changes between the two samples while result-counts is still null. Paste both JSON samples into the return. A return that only shows a completed-run status (result-counts populated) is INSUFFICIENT and will be rejected — that is exactly the mistake that shipped this bug.

FILE: scripts/conformance/06-run-sonobuoy.sh only.

DONE-WHEN:
- A healthy >15min conformance run completes without being killed by the stall-watchdog.
- A genuinely stalled run (no progress.completed/msg change for 15min) is still killed and partial results retrieved.
- Worker return includes two mid-run 'sonobuoy status --json' samples proving progress.* advances while result-counts is null.
close_reason: stall-watchdog keys on progress.completed/msg; mayor captured live mid-run samples proving result-counts is null while progress.msg advances; PR #532

title: fix(apiserver): invoke mutating and validating webhooks during admission
description: u7s stores ValidatingWebhookConfiguration and MutatingWebhookConfiguration objects (CRUD works) but never consults them during admission. When a resource is created or mutated, the apiserver must look up matching webhook configurations, call each webhook's clientConfig.url or service endpoint, and apply the result (deny or mutate). This is the core admission enforcement path. Without it: mutating webhooks never fire (tested by should mutate custom resource, should mutate pod and apply defaults after mutation, should mutate everything except skip-me configmaps), validating webhooks never deny (should be able to deny custom resource creation). Observed in temp/e2e/0612-1835-admissionwebhook junit_01.xml: 5+ failures directly caused by this. Note: mayor-rzmf (in_progress) tracked a symptom (43s timeout) of this same gap but framed it as a networking issue. Close mayor-rzmf as superseded when this bead is filed. Key files: crates/apiserver/src/admission.rs (WebhookEntry, matching logic), crates/apiserver/src/handlers/ (PUT/POST handlers where admission must be called). The webhook call itself requires mTLS via konnectivity (service-backed webhooks) or direct HTTPS (url-backed). Done-when: should mutate custom resource and should be able to deny custom resource creation pass in the AdmissionWebhook conformance suite.
notes: Scope: webhook invocation only — call matching webhooks on create/update/delete, apply mutation result, enforce denial. Do NOT tackle: matchConditions CEL enforcement (mayor-zbqc), timeout error shape (mayor-scgr), attach denial (mayor-iv82, depends on this). Today's run (0621-1116) shows 6 failures from missing invocation: mutate custom resource x2, mutate everything except skip-me, mutate pod+defaults, deny custom resource. Failure shape: mutations produce only mutation-start label, never mutation-stage-1 — confirms webhooks called zero times.
close_reason: PR #543 opened. Admission webhooks wired into all 6 CR write handlers (create_cr, create_cr_namespaced, replace_cr, replace_cr_namespaced, patch_cr, patch_cr_namespaced). Mutations fire (mutation-stage-1 lands), denials enforced. Regression tests: create_cr_namespaced_calls_admission_ignore_policy_passes_through, create_cr_namespaced_calls_validating_admission_fail_policy_denies, create_cr_calls_admission_fail_policy_denies_cluster_scoped. Follow-ons: mayor-zbqc (matchConditions), mayor-scgr (timeout shape), mayor-iv82 (attach denial).

title: fix(watch): labelSelector watch sends events to wrong watchers — fan-out filtering bug
description:
Test: [sig-api-machinery] Watchers should observe add, update, and delete watch notifications on configmaps (watch.go:60)
Duration: 0.044s (immediate). Observed in temp/e2e-job-c77fffa5.log line 2950.

The test opens three watch streams: label A, label B, label A-or-B. After creating configmap-B, the label-A watcher receives an unexpected ADDED event for configmap-B. This means the server-side label selector filtering on watch streams is not working — events are being broadcast to all watchers regardless of their labelSelector.

From the log: 'Unexpected watch notification observed: {ADDED &ConfigMap{...labels:{watch-this-configmap:multiple-watchers-B}...}}' on the watcher that only asked for label A.

The watch handler in crates/apiserver/src/handlers/watch.rs must filter broadcast events against each watcher's labelSelector before emitting. If the filter is missing or evaluating incorrectly, all events fan out to all watchers.

Acceptance criteria: a watch with labelSelector=A does not receive events for objects matching only labelSelector=B.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #514: implemented DoesNotExist/Exists/NotEquals label selector operators in parse_label_selector (generic.rs) and object_matches_label_selector (watch.rs). KCM's !headless EPS watch now filters correctly; svc-latency hang should be resolved.

title: fix(store): continue token TTL not enforced — expired after 973s instead of 60s
description:
Test: [sig-api-machinery] Servers with support for API chunking should support continue listing from the last key if the original version has been compacted away (chunking.go:144)
Duration: 57s. Observed in temp/e2e-job-c77fffa5.log line 17.

The test creates a paginated list, gets a continue token, then waits for it to expire (TTL=60s). After 60s it retries and expects an error 'continue token expired'. Instead u7s served the token as valid for 973 seconds (chunking.go:177: 'issued 973s ago (TTL is 60s)').

The continue token encodes a key and a timestamp (base64 JSON: {k: ..., t: <unix>}). The TTL check must compare the encoded timestamp against current time and reject tokens older than 60s. Either (a) the TTL check is missing entirely, (b) the timestamp in the token is being set to epoch/zero instead of now, or (c) the check uses wall-clock incorrectly.

Acceptance criteria: a continue token issued more than 60s ago is rejected with an appropriate error; the chunking conformance test passes.
close_reason: PR #518 merged: preserve cursor key in expired continue token 410 response.

title: fix(conformance): DNS /etc/hosts test burns 614s — pod lookup returns 404 during exec result read
description:
Test: [sig-network] DNS should provide /etc/hosts entries for the cluster (dns.go:130)
Duration: 614 seconds (10+ minutes) before failing.
Observed in: temp/e2e-job-c77fffa5.log line 1508.

The test creates a pod then polls GET /api/v1/namespaces/dns-2235/pods/dns-test-99675610-b3d2-4d11-af4a-b660a620ab98 every 5 seconds for 600 iterations. Every poll returns 'the server could not find the requested resource'. The pod was successfully created (dns_common.go shows it was submitted) but subsequent GETs 404.

Note: WebSocket exec IS implemented. The 404 is on a plain pod GET, not exec. Likely cause: the pod was created in namespace dns-2235 but the GET is hitting a different resource path, OR the namespace itself was garbage-collected prematurely, OR there is a case sensitivity / name encoding issue in the pod name (UUID in name). Investigate why GET /api/v1/namespaces/dns-2235/pods/<uuid-name> returns 404 for a pod that was successfully POSTed.

Acceptance criteria: the DNS /etc/hosts test fails fast (under 30s) or passes; it does not burn 600s polling a 404.
notes: Worker investigation confirmed: routing is correct (UUID-named pod GETs reach pod handler, not fallback). The 614s burn is because dns_common.go:495 tries to exec into pods that never reach Running state — the pod is created but never scheduled/started by kubelet. Root cause is pod lifecycle/exec infrastructure, not API server store key mismatch. PR #522 adds a routing regression test. Reassigning focus: the real fix requires pods to reach Running (kubelet scheduling or exec subresource gap). See mayor-pbwj for exec angle.
close_reason: PR #522 opened. Investigation: routing is correct (test proves it). Production fallback message source unidentified via static analysis. Test documents routing behavior as regression guard.

title: fix(scripts): add --port flag for apiserver port isolation between parallel workers
close_reason: PR #510 merged; --port flag added to u7s-start.sh, lima-start.sh, 04-start-kcm.sh; dispatch-prompt-template.md updated with port-assignment model

title: fix(conformance): StatefulSet scale-to-0 during rolling update races; KCM recreates pod causing 10-min teardown hang
description:
When a StatefulSet is scale(0) while a rolling update is in progress (image change + replicas bump happened 80ms earlier), the KCM recreates the pod 7ms after its hard-delete. The recreated pod runs for 10 minutes until namespace teardown, causing the e2e Scale() wait loop to time out and panic at rest.go:170.

## Context
Observed in 2026-06-11 run. apiserver.log:1419: POST /pods/test-ss-0 → 201 at 01:10:15.506, only 7ms after hard-delete at 01:10:15.499. KCM then does NOT delete the excess pod despite spec.replicas=0. Pattern repeats in statefulset-712 and statefulset-1452. Hypothesis: rolling-update reconcile was queued before the Scale(0) MODIFIED event was processed by the StatefulSet informer; it ran with stale spec.replicas=2 and pods=[] → created pod. KCM logs needed to confirm.
acceptance_criteria: A Scale(0) issued during a rolling update results in 0 pods within 30s. The KCM does not recreate any pod after scale-to-zero. Test should not hang.
notes:
DIAGNOSTIC RUN 2 (2026-06-11 ~13:00): Default-verbosity KCM log shows:

1. Original pod-recreation race (statefulset-7698, 01:10 run) DID NOT reproduce in the 10:42 run. Either timing-dependent or fixed by recent commits.

2. NEW SYMPTOM confirmed: After 3x 'Pod already exists' 409s during initial ss-0 creation race, KCM silently abandons the rolling update for statefulset-2510 for 10 minutes. KCM log shows NO entries for statefulset-2510 between 19:41:55 and 19:52:05. KCM did process MODIFIED event from the PATCH (apiserver lines 941-942 show GET + PUT status), but decided nothing to do.

3. ConsistencyStore errors are systemic: 'read version N is not as new as written version N+1 for statefulsets.apps' fire after every status write. This is likely expected behavior (informer lags one RV behind each write). Not the root cause.

4. WATCH DELIVERY CONFIRMED OK: KCM received MODIFIED event from PATCH and immediately read/wrote status. Event delivery is not the bug.

5. KEY UNANSWERED QUESTION: What did the KCM's pod lister show for ss-0 image during the rolling-update reconcile at 19:42:05? If ss-0 appears to have the NEW image already (stale cache from the creation race), the rolling update controller would see nothing to do. Need --v=4 to confirm.

BLOCKER: Worker could not restart KCM with --v=4 due to script execution constraints. Next diagnostic must start KCM directly via limactl shell (not via 04-start-kcm.sh) with --v=4 flag.

NEXT STEP: Dispatch second diagnostic worker that:
1. Uses run-all.sh --reset to set up cluster
2. Kills KCM inside VM via limactl shell
3. Restarts KCM manually via limactl shell with --v=4 and same flags as 04-start-kcm.sh
4. Runs --focus 'rolling updates' test
5. Extracts verbose log lines showing what image/spec the KCM saw in the reconcile at the critical moment
close_reason: Closed

title: fix(apiserver/proto): StatefulSet proto decoder drops spec.replicas=0 causing default to 1
description:
The StatefulSet proto decoder in crates/apiserver/src/proto.rs skips writing spec.replicas to the output JSON when the proto value is 0 (proto3 treats 0 as the default/absent value). This means a proto-encoded PUT with spec.replicas=0 stores a JSON object with no replicas field. default_statefulset then sees spec.replicas.is_null()==true and sets it to 1, permanently corrupting the stored spec.

## Context
Affected code: proto.rs:2692 and proto.rs:4229. Both use: if spec.replicas != 0 { ... }. Fix: write replicas unconditionally when decoding proto StatefulSet bodies. Does NOT affect the 2026-06-11 test run (that test used JSON PUT), but WILL corrupt any proto-encoded scale-to-zero request (e.g., kubectl scale --replicas=0).
acceptance_criteria: A proto-encoded PUT with spec.replicas=0 stores JSON with replicas:0; a subsequent GET returns replicas:0; default_statefulset does not change it.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #509: spec.replicas written unconditionally in all workload proto decoders (StatefulSet, Deployment, ReplicaSet, ReplicationController)

title: write_vap_status overwrites status on PATCH /status subresource (breaks conformance)
description:
The PATCH /status conformance test at validatingadmissionpolicy.go:601 patches status.conditions with a custom condition (PatchStatusFailed), then asserts the response contains that condition.

write_vap_status (resource.rs:1903) unconditionally overwrites obj_body[status] with a hardcoded Ready condition after every store write. It is called at:
- resource.rs:311 (create_resource)
- resource.rs:435 (patch_resource)

When the test does PATCH /validatingadmissionpolicies/<name>/status, the patch applies the new condition, writes to DB, then write_vap_status overwrites the status with {conditions: [{type: Ready}]}. The response is missing the PatchStatusFailed condition, so the test fails.

Fix: do NOT call write_vap_status from the /status subresource handler. The /status handler must honor whatever the client sends as-is. Only call write_vap_status from the main resource create/update path (not /status).

To distinguish: the /status path can be identified by the subresource parameter or by context. Looking at resource.rs, the patch handler at line 390 handles both main object and /status patches — need to check how it knows it is handling /status.
close_reason: PR #503 opened — removed write_vap_status from patch_resource_status in status.rs; added regression test vap_patch_status_preserves_client_conditions_not_overwritten_by_write_vap_status

title: VAP denial returns 403 Forbidden instead of 422 Invalid (breaks conformance)
description:
The conformance test at validatingadmissionpolicy.go:120 and :270 polls for the marker Deployment to be denied using apierrors.IsInvalid (HTTP 422). Our VAP evaluation (admission.rs:2314) returns Status::forbidden (403) instead. The test treats any non-422 error as unexpected and fails immediately.

Real Kubernetes VAP behavior: when a validation expression evaluates to false, the denial status uses reason=Invalid (HTTP 422) by default. The spec.validations[].reason field can override this — valid values are 'FieldValueInvalid', 'FieldValueForbidden', 'FieldValueRequired', 'FieldValueDuplicate'; default is 'Invalid' which maps to HTTP 422.

Fix needed:
- In admission.rs around line 2297-2314: when reason is 'Forbidden', return Status::forbidden (403). Otherwise (default, or reason='Invalid'/'FieldValueInvalid'/etc.), return Status::unprocessable_entity (422) with reason=Invalid.
- Update the vap_denial_produces_well_formed_status_error_with_code_403 test to expect 422 when no reason is specified.
- Also audit: the validation.reason field should map to the appropriate HTTP code per https://pkg.go.dev/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/api/errors

This is the root cause of the remaining replicas>1 and variables.replicas>1 conformance failures.
close_reason: merged as PR #502

title: fix(admission): spec.replicas > 1 CEL expression evaluates to false in VAP
description:
VAP conformance test: [sig-auth] ValidatingAdmissionPolicy can restrict access using the expression

Two failing test variants:
1. expression 'variables.replicas > 1' evaluated to false
   (uses CEL variable referencing spec.replicas via params)
2. expression 'object.spec.replicas > 1' evaluated to false
   (direct object field access)

Both evaluate to false when the admission request has spec.replicas=2 (set via kubectl scale).
kubectl round-trip works correctly (GET shows spec.replicas=2 after scale).
The CEL evaluator is seeing a different value — likely 0 or 1.

Root cause hypothesis: the proto decoder for Deployment drops or misreads spec.replicas.
PR #496 (mayor-fmqw) fixed spec.replicas preservation in proto decoders but the VAP
admission path may be re-decoding the object from a different source (e.g. re-reading from
store after write, or using the proto wire bytes directly) that still loses the field.

Done-when: the conformance test '[sig-auth] ValidatingAdmissionPolicy can restrict access'
passes without the 'expression evaluated to false' failure in both variants.

Files likely involved:
- crates/apiserver/src/proto.rs (proto decoder for Deployment/ReplicaSet)
- crates/apiserver/src/admission.rs (where CEL evaluator receives the object)
- crates/apiserver/src/handlers/resource.rs (create_resource / replace_resource admission path)

Regression test: unit test asserting that after a Deployment with spec.replicas=2 is stored
and retrieved, the CEL expression 'object.spec.replicas > 1' evaluates to true.
close_reason: PR #501 merged — regression test for spec.replicas store round-trip

title: fix(namespace): namespace with CRD group hangs on deletion — KCM GC watch prevents drain
description:
## Symptom

When a VAP conformance test namespace is deleted, the e2e framework hangs waiting for the namespace to disappear. Root cause: the test creates a CRD (e.g. crontabs.stable.validating-admission-policy-1392.example.com) during the test. KCM registers a quota evaluator and cluster-wide watch on this CRD. When the namespace controller tries to drain namespace 1392, it must list/delete all CRD instances — but because the CRD still exists after the test, KCM's GC controller keeps re-queuing the namespace. The namespace never reaches phase Terminating and is never removed.

Observed in two consecutive VAP focus runs (2026-06-09). The e2e binary finishes all 4 tests (all Timeline blocks closed) but hangs waiting for namespace deletion before reporting to sonobuoy. Sonobuoy then prints '...' forever.

## Location

crates/apiserver/src/handlers/crd.rs — CRD delete / namespace delete interaction.
Also check crates/apiserver/src/handlers/resource.rs namespace termination path.

The fix should ensure that when a namespace is deleted, any CRDs whose group is scoped to that namespace (i.e. group contains the namespace name) are also deleted, or that the namespace drain does not block on CRD instance listing when the CRD itself is being removed.

## Done when

title: fix(tls): kubelet watch reconnection fails with ECDSA verification error after ~70min — all kubelet-to-apiserver calls break
notes:
Systemic TLS reconnection bug found during kubelet investigation cluster (mayor-06h6, mayor-5v9l, mayor-xi62).

SYMPTOMS:
- All kubelet-to-apiserver calls fail with: 'tls: failed to verify certificate: x509: ECDSA verification failure'
- Initial connections succeed; failure triggers after watch timeout expiry forces reconnection (~70min uptime)
- All kubelet status PATCHes fail (probe results detected locally but never reported)
- All kubelet ConfigMap reflectors die (watch reconnection fails)
- Probe detection works locally but results cannot reach apiserver

KEY LOG LINE:
  Jun 08 15:03:40 status_manager.go:1164 'Failed to get status for pod'
    err='Get .../pods/ss-0: tls: failed to verify certificate:
    x509: certificate signed by unknown authority (possibly because of x509: ECDSA verification failure)'

CERT FINGERPRINT ANOMALY:
  CA cert, leaf cert, and kubeconfig all share identical fingerprint: EC:96:52:...:34:A3
  Initial connections succeed, so the cert is valid at first. Reconnection fails.

HYPOTHESES:
1. Go TLS session cache: on reconnect, Go presents a cached session ticket but the server cannot resume it, and the fallback full-handshake fails ECDSA verification
2. Client-go watch reconnection creates a new TLS client that does not trust the CA (cert pinning issue)
3. The kubelet-serving cert is self-signed per-node; the apiserver CA cert used for kubelet verification is wrong after cert rotation

title: fix(admission): MutatingAdmissionPolicy (CEL-based) not implemented — test infinite-loops creating marker deployments waiting for mutation that never happens
notes:
OBSERVED BEHAVIOUR (2026-06-07, full conformance run e8a946):

1. e2e log ends at 11:03:04 UTC after DNS test failure in namespace dns-2781.
2. Immediately after (11:03:18 UTC) the apiserver receives namespace setup requests for mutating-admission-policy-2838.
3. For the next 4+ hours the e2e process polls TWO pods every 10 seconds:
   - marker-deployment-6676fc7d87-6397a (GET every 10s)
   - marker-deployment-57dd768bb-c07f2 (GET every 10s)
4. The test progressively creates NEW marker Deployments (5 total over 4h), suggesting it creates new variants when the current one doesn't show the expected mutation after some timeout.
5. No log output from the e2e binary during this entire period — ginkgo STEP/It lines stop after 11:03.

ROOT CAUSE: The conformance test for MutatingAdmissionPolicy (CEL-based policy, separate from webhook admission) creates a MutatingAdmissionPolicy resource and then creates marker Deployments expecting them to be mutated by the policy. u7s does not implement MutatingAdmissionPolicy — the policy is stored but never evaluated during admission. PRIOR OCCURRENCE: Same leak pattern seen with validating-admission-policy-3797 namespace in previous full runs.

REPRODUCTION STEPS:
1. Check if MutatingAdmissionPolicy resource type is served:
   kubectl get --raw /apis/admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1alpha1 | jq '.resources[] | .name'
2. Create a MutatingAdmissionPolicy pointing at Deployments with a CEL mutation (e.g. add a label)
3. Create a Deployment — check if the label was added
4. Expected: label present. Actual: label absent (policy not evaluated)

1. MutatingAdmissionPolicy resource must be stored and served (check if it is already — it was failing with invalid JSON in 0605-1344 run, bead mayor-blpb fixed some proto decoders but may not have covered MutatingAdmissionPolicy)
2. The admission pipeline must evaluate MutatingAdmissionPolicy objects against each incoming CREATE/UPDATE and apply the CEL-specified mutations
3. Unit tests: create a MutatingAdmissionPolicy, create a resource, assert the mutation was applied
4. The test uses this test namespace prefix: mutating-admission-policy-*

title: fix(watch): namespace deletion Watch stream deadlocks e2e framework — 410 Compacted on long-lived watches loses DELETED events, blocking namespace cleanup forever
notes:
Root cause confirmed from 12h conformance run. The e2e framework opens a Watch on namespaces (field selector metadata.name=webhook-622) and waits for the DELETED event. After 12+ hours of running, the Watch ring buffer compacts (410 Compacted). The framework tries to relist — but the namespace no longer exists after the relist, so there is nothing to watch. The framework goroutine blocks forever. The #423 Watch broadcast lag fix improved resilience but did not fix the case where the object being watched is deleted while the Watch stream is in a 410-relist cycle. Fix: when a namespace is deleted and there are active Watch streams for that namespace (or the parent namespaces collection), ensure a DELETED WatchEvent is emitted even after a compaction cycle. This requires persisting the deletion tombstone long enough for reconnecting watchers to see it. See crates/store/src/lib.rs watch() and the Compacted/relist path. title: fix(apiserver): strategic-merge-patch $patch:delete entries accumulate in pod status fields — kubelet detects spurious changes and recreates sandbox
notes:
Discovered during kube-proxy deployment (PR #406). When a pod uses hostNetwork:true and the kubelet patches pod status (spec.podIPs, status.podIPs), the u7s strategic-merge-patch handler stores the $patch:delete directives literally instead of applying them. On each reconcile the kubelet sees podIPs has changed, recreates the sandbox, killing the container.

Effect: any pod that receives repeated status patches with strategic-merge-patch semantics on array fields (podIPs, containerStatuses) will be continuously restarted by the kubelet. kube-proxy is the clearest example — it gets killed before it can start.

Workaround in #406: run kube-proxy as a systemd service inside the VM, bypassing the apiserver pod lifecycle entirely.

Root cause: the strategic-merge-patch implementation in patch_pod_status (crates/apiserver/src/handlers/pods.rs) or the general patch handler does not correctly apply $patch:delete directives for array items. Instead of removing the item, it stores the directive as a literal JSON object in the array.

Fix: in the strategic-merge-patch handler, when processing arrays, recognize and apply $patch:delete directives (remove array items matching the merge key) rather than storing them literally. Reference: https://github.com/kubernetes/community/blob/master/contributors/devel/sig-api-machinery/strategic-merge-patch.md

Once fixed, kube-proxy can be migrated from systemd service back to a proper kube-system DaemonSet (file follow-on bead after fix is verified).
close_reason: PR #409 opened

title: feat(infra): run kube-proxy as DaemonSet in kube-system to enable ClusterIP routing
notes:
Without kube-proxy, ClusterIPs (10.96.0.0/12) are unreachable from pods. CoreDNS resolves service names to ClusterIPs but nothing routes that traffic to the actual pod IPs. This blocks: ingress controllers, Gateway API implementations, any pod doing HTTP to another Service, and proper webhook routing.

We already have one manual DNAT rule for 10.96.0.1:443 → apiserver in lima-start.sh. kube-proxy generalises this for all Services.

Implementation: add kube-proxy as a DaemonSet in kube-system, alongside konnectivity-agent. The image is registry.k8s.io/kube-proxy:v${K8S_VERSION}. It needs:
- hostNetwork: true (needs access to the node's iptables)
- privileged: true or at least NET_ADMIN capability
- A kubeconfig pointing at the apiserver (can reuse the same kubeconfig as kubelet)
- ConfigMap with kube-proxy config (mode: iptables, clusterCIDR: 10.85.0.0/16)

Similar to the konnectivity-agent DaemonSet approach. The kube-proxy pod programs iptables DNAT rules in the VM for every Service ClusterIP, making them routable from within the cluster.

Once in place: in-cluster ClusterIP traffic works, ingress/gateway controllers can forward to Services, webhook services may be reachable by ClusterIP (still need konnectivity for Mac→cluster traffic). The danger_accept_invalid_hostnames workaround in admission.rs may or may not be removable -- konnectivity still routes by pod IP so hostname check still mismatches unless we switch back to service DNS URL.

Add kube-proxy start to scripts/conformance/lima-start.sh alongside konnectivity-agent. Use same Secret/kubeconfig approach. Node name: lima-node.

Version alignment: kube-proxy version must match kubelet version (matrix: 1.34.8, 1.35.5, 1.36.1). Use the same version variable as KCM.

title: fix(ci): cache kubectl and kubelet binaries in smoke.yaml to avoid pkgs.k8s.io rate limit 403s
notes:
smoke.yaml installs kubectl and kubelet via 'apt-get install' from pkgs.k8s.io on every CI run. These downloads get 403 rate-limit errors causing frequent CI failures (seen on at least PRs #393, #399, #400, #401, #404).

Fix: add 'actions/cache' steps before the apt-install steps to cache the installed binary paths. Both kubectl and kubelet are installed to /usr/bin/kubectl and /usr/bin/kubelet respectively. Cache key: '<binary>-<matrix.k8s>-<runner.arch>'.

Pattern to use:
  - uses: actions/cache@v4
    id: cache-kubectl
    with:
      path: /usr/bin/kubectl
      key: kubectl-${{ matrix.k8s }}-${{ runner.arch }}
  - name: Install kubectl
    if: steps.cache-kubectl.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
    run: ... (existing install step)

The 'if: steps.cache-kubectl.outputs.cache-hit != true' guard skips the apt install when the binary is cached. This is the standard pattern for caching installed binaries in GitHub Actions.

Also add caching for cri-o in the kubelet job (apt install) -- that's another potential rate-limit target.

KCM (04-start-kcm.sh) already has 'if [ ! -f KCM_BINARY ]' check so it naturally skips re-downloading -- but the GitHub Actions cache for ~/.cache/u7s/kcm/ should also be added for the kcm CI job (test.yaml) to persist across runs.

File to change: .github/workflows/smoke.yaml (main target)
Optionally: .github/workflows/test.yaml (for kcm cache)

No Rust changes needed.

title: fix(admission): reqwest mTLS identity fails against konnectivity proxy despite valid cert — curl succeeds with same cert
notes:
Confirmed via curl: mTLS with admin cert against konnectivity proxy (127.0.0.1:8135 https) works perfectly -- TLS handshake succeeds, CONNECT tunnel established.

curl flags that work:
  --proxy https://127.0.0.1:8135
  --proxy-cacert $WORKDIR/ca.pem
  --proxy-cert /tmp/admin_cert.pem  (from kubeconfig client-certificate-data, base64 -d)
  --proxy-key /tmp/admin_key.pem    (from kubeconfig client-key-data, base64 -d)

But reqwest::Proxy::all() + reqwest::Identity::from_pem() gets 'remote error: tls: unknown certificate' from the konnectivity-server.

Cert verified: admin cert is signed by cluster CA (openssl verify: OK).
konnectivity-server uses --server-ca-cert=ca.pem (same CA).

Investigation path:
1. In build_webhook_call_client (crates/apiserver/src/admission.rs), log the PEM bytes being passed to Identity::from_pem -- first line, length, whether it starts with -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE----- or not.
2. Check if AppState.webhook_identity_pem is actually set: add tracing::info! in state.rs new_with_config where webhook_identity_pem is assigned.
3. Try building the reqwest client with explicit cert+key as two separate items (reqwest Identity can sometimes require specific ordering).
4. If the identity bytes look correct, try a minimal Rust test program that connects to konnectivity proxy using the same cert -- to rule out reqwest version issues on macOS.

The admin cert+key come from tls_material.admin_cert_pem + tls_material.admin_key_pem (concatenated in main.rs line ~210). The PEM format should be CERTIFICATE + PRIVATE KEY (rcgen uses PKCS8 format for private keys).

All relevant files: crates/apiserver/src/admission.rs (build_webhook_call_client), crates/apiserver/src/state.rs (build_webhook_client, AppState.webhook_identity_pem), crates/apiserver/src/main.rs (webhook_identity_pem construction).

title: fix(admission): use per-webhook caBundle for TLS verification — build reqwest::Client per webhook call using clientConfig.caBundle
notes:
The webhook_client in AppState is built once with tls_certs_only([cluster_ca_cert]). Webhook pods present their own TLS cert (from VWC clientConfig.caBundle), not the cluster CA — the VWC is created dynamically by clients and we cannot control which CA they use. Our shared client rejects the webhook cert → konnectivity CONNECT tunnel closes immediately → webhook fails.

Fix: in run_validating_webhooks and run_mutating_webhooks, instead of using state.webhook_client, build a per-call reqwest::Client that:
1. Reads caBundle (base64-encoded PEM CA cert) from the WebhookEntry.client_config.ca_bundle field (currently not deserialized — need to add to WebhookClientConfig struct)
2. Decodes the base64 bytes and builds reqwest::Certificate::from_pem()
3. Builds a reqwest::Client with that single cert as trust anchor
4. Also sets danger_accept_invalid_hostnames(true) because we connect via 127.0.0.1 (proxy tunnel) but the cert is issued for the service DNS name (e.g. e2e-test-webhook.webhook-N.svc)
5. Falls back to state.webhook_client if caBundle is absent (uses system/cluster roots)

Files to change:
- crates/apiserver/src/admission.rs: add ca_bundle field to WebhookClientConfig, build per-call client in dispatch path
- crates/apiserver/src/handlers/authorization.rs: no change needed (TokenReview, different path)

The WebhookClientConfig struct currently only has url and service fields. Add:
  ca_bundle: Option<String>  (base64 PEM bytes)

In call_webhook, change signature to accept Option<&[u8]> ca_pem and build the client inline.

Regression test: unit test that a webhook with a self-signed caBundle can authenticate (mock server with that cert).

pkill u7s-apiserver is whitelisted in settings.json — workers can restart the server. After implementing, worker must: cargo build --release, pkill u7s-apiserver, restart, run sonobuoy focused on AdmissionWebhook, confirm Passed:20 Failed:0.

title: fix(konnectivity): wire agent auth and server cert for http-connect mode
notes:
Three remaining gaps to make konnectivity http-connect mode work end-to-end:

1. konnectivity-server cert: the server's --cluster-cert must have 'host.lima.internal' as a SAN so the agent can verify TLS. Currently u7s-start.sh uses the CA cert (ca.pem) directly which has no SAN. Fix: generate a dedicated konnectivity-server.crt using 'openssl req + x509' with -sha256 and a [v3_req] extension block containing 'subjectAltName = IP:127.0.0.1,DNS:host.lima.internal'. Also need --server-ca-cert and --server-cert/--server-key for TCP mode. See investigate logs: cert must use ecdsa-with-SHA256 (LibreSSL on Mac defaults to SHA-1 if -sha256 not specified).

2. Agent kubeconfig: the konnectivity-agent uses --kubeconfig to get a SA token to send to konnectivity-server for auth. Currently the agent uses /etc/kubelet-kubeconfig (system:node identity) but konnectivity-server expects 'kube-system/konnectivity-agent' SA. Fix: (a) create kube-system/konnectivity-agent SA in lima-start.sh via kubectl, (b) generate a token via 'kubectl create token konnectivity-agent -n kube-system', (c) write a dedicated /etc/konnectivity-agent-kubeconfig with that token, (d) pass that kubeconfig to the agent.

3. Agent restart: kubelet-reconnect.sh and lima-start.sh need to pass --kubeconfig=/etc/konnectivity-agent-kubeconfig to the agent (not /etc/kubelet-kubeconfig).

Note: the konnectivity-server in http-connect mode still uses gRPC for the agent port (8132). The mode flag only changes the frontend (apiserver→server) port 8135 protocol. The agent binary does not need to be rebuilt — it always speaks gRPC to the server's agent port. Confirmed: 'Authentication context was not found in metadata' = agent not sending SA token. Once SA+kubeconfig are wired, the tunnel should work and AdmissionWebhook should pass 20/20.

Files to modify: scripts/u7s-start.sh (cert generation), scripts/conformance/lima-start.sh (SA creation + agent kubeconfig), scripts/kubelet-reconnect.sh (agent kubeconfig).
