title: fix(proto): Probe handler fields (exec/httpGet/tcpSocket) not decoded — kubelet reports 'missing probe handler'
description:
AdmissionWebhook test now gets past the revision annotation step but fails with 'Readiness probe errored: missing probe handler'. Our Probe prost struct decodes timing fields (initialDelaySeconds, etc) but not the handler sub-messages (exec, httpGet, tcpSocket). When pods are created via protobuf with httpGet/exec readiness probes, the stored pod has probe timing but no handler — kubelet sees a probe with no action to execute.

From api-core-v1-generated.proto Probe message:
- field 1 = exec (ExecAction: field 1 = command repeated string)
- field 2 = httpGet (HTTPGetAction: field 1 = path string, field 2 = port IntOrString, field 3 = host string, field 6 = scheme string)
- field 4 = tcpSocket (TCPSocketAction: field 1 = port IntOrString, field 2 = host string)
- field 11 = grpc (GRPCAction: field 1 = port int32, field 2 = service string)

Fix: extend Probe struct with exec (field 1), httpGet (field 2), tcpSocket (field 4), grpc (field 11). Add corresponding prost structs for ExecAction, HTTPGetAction, TCPSocketAction, GRPCAction. Include them in probe_to_json output.
close_reason: PR #385 opened — decode Probe handler sub-messages (exec/httpGet/tcpSocket/grpc) so kubelet no longer reports 'missing probe handler'

title: fix(apiserver): KCM deployment controller does not set deployment.kubernetes.io/revision annotation — Deployment spec.template.spec now stored but annotation still missing
description:
After PRs #381 (strip creationTimestamp:null) and #383 (decode PodTemplateSpec.spec), the Deployment template and RS template are now identical (EqualIgnoreHash should return true). BUT KCM's deployment controller still does not PATCH the Deployment to set deployment.kubernetes.io/revision=1 annotation.

Evidence:
- test-spec2 Deployment: spec.template.spec IS present (containers=[busybox])
- RS spec.template.spec also present, same containers
- diff of templates shows only pod-template-hash difference (which EqualIgnoreHash ignores)
- KCM logs show NO deployment controller activity, NO errors
- KCM has 60 active connections to apiserver

Hypothesis: KCM's deployment controller is running but skips the annotation-setting PATCH for an unknown reason. Possibly:
1. Our Deployment response is missing a required field that causes KCM to bail early
2. The watch events for the Deployment are malformed
3. KCM sees the Deployment in a state that makes it think annotation is already set

Investigation: add RUST_LOG=debug logging to capture what PATCH requests KCM sends for Deployments. Build with debug logging, restart, create a test Deployment, watch apiserver log for any PATCH to /apis/apps/v1/.../deployments/test-name.
close_reason: PR #384 opened: fix propagates RS revision annotation to owning Deployment on create; regression test added; awaiting live verification after server restart

title: fix(proto): PodTemplateSpec missing spec.containers — stored Deployment template has spec:null, EqualIgnoreHash fails
description:
AdmissionWebhook still fails at 19/20. creationTimestamp:null is now stripped (#381) but spec.template.spec is still null in stored Deployments.

Evidence: kubectl get deployment test-check2 -o json | jq '.spec.template.spec' returns null. The RS (created by KCM) has real containers. EqualIgnoreHash sees Deployment.spec.template.spec=null vs RS.spec.template.spec={containers:[...]} → not equal → FindNewReplicaSet returns nil.

Root cause: AppsPodTemplateSpec in proto.rs only decodes metadata (field 1). Field 2 (spec = PodSpec) is not decoded. When a Deployment is submitted via protobuf, the pod spec (containers, volumes, etc) is in PodTemplateSpec.spec but we don't capture it.

Fix: extend AppsPodTemplateSpec to pass through spec as raw JSON. The simplest approach: add a catch-all 'spec' field using prost bytes or use a passthrough JSON approach. Since we don't need to reason about PodSpec fields for the Deployment path (KCM handles pod creation), we just need to store the full spec verbatim.

The challenge: PodSpec is extremely complex (50+ fields). Rather than decoding all of PodSpec, the fix should pass through spec as an opaque JSON blob. Check how decode_deployment_proto reconstructs the JSON — we may be able to capture the raw bytes for the spec field and insert them as-is into the JSON output.
close_reason: PR #383 opened — AppsPodTemplateSpec now decodes field 2 (PodSpec), spec.template.spec is no longer null in stored Deployments

title: fix(apiserver): pod-template-hash mismatch — apiserver mutates pod template after KCM hashes it, FindNewReplicaSet returns nil
description:
AdmissionWebhook test stuck at 19/20. Root cause: KCM's deployment controller computes pod-template-hash from the submitted pod template, creates RS with that hash. Our apiserver then mutates the stored Deployment's pod template (inject SA token volume, set defaultMode=420 on volumes, etc). The stored template differs from what KCM hashed. FindNewReplicaSet recomputes hash from the stored template, gets a different value, returns nil. Test logs: 'new replicaset for deployment is yet to be created'.

Evidence: RS exists with correct owner reference and pod-template-hash=865c99bfc7, but Deployment.spec.template.metadata.labels has no pod-template-hash. FindNewReplicaSet looks for RSes whose pod-template-hash matches the hash of the Deployment's current spec.template — but our stored spec.template was mutated after hashing.

Fix: apply pod template mutations (SA volume injection, defaultMode defaults) BEFORE storing the Deployment object in the create path. This way KCM hashes the same template that gets stored. The mutation currently happens in inject_sa_token_volume and apply_volume_defaults — these should run before the Deployment is stored, not just before Pod creation.

Alternative: do not mutate Deployment.spec.template at all — only mutate the Pods when they're created by KCM. This is actually the correct Kubernetes semantics: Deployment spec is stored verbatim, pod mutations happen at pod admission time.
notes: REVISED: Deployment template mutations are not the issue. Two real causes of EqualIgnoreHash failure: (1) Deployment template has 'creationTimestamp: null' in metadata (added by our JSON serialization of ObjectMeta) but RS template does not — KCM strips null creationTimestamp when creating the RS. (2) Deployment.spec.template.spec.containers is null/missing because our proto decoder for DeploymentSpec (field 3 = PodTemplateSpec) only decodes metadata, not spec.containers. Fix: (a) Strip null creationTimestamp from pod template metadata when storing, OR ensure EqualIgnoreHash comparison ignores it. (b) Extend PodTemplateSpec decoder to include spec.containers so the stored Deployment template matches what KCM creates in the RS.
close_reason: PR #380 opened: regression test guards against SA volume injection into Deployment pod templates; code analysis confirmed inject_sa_token_volume and apply_pod_create_defaults are already correctly isolated to the Pod create path only

title: fix(apiserver): KCM deployment controller PATCH to set revision annotation not persisting
description:
AdmissionWebhook test waits for deployment.kubernetes.io/revision annotation on the Deployment (set by KCM deployment controller). The annotation never appears — KCM's PATCH is not persisting.

Manual kubectl patch works fine. KCM uses strategic merge patch or server-side apply to set the annotation. Check if our PATCH handler for Deployments (apps/v1) correctly merges metadata.annotations when sent as part of a strategic merge patch body from KCM.

The RS has deployment.kubernetes.io/revision=1 (correct), but the Deployment itself has annotations=null. KCM should PATCH the Deployment to add the revision annotation after creating the RS.
notes: REVISED DIAGNOSIS: The RS is created and owned by the Deployment. FindNewReplicaSet returns nil because the RS pod-template-hash doesn't match the Deployment's current pod template hash. This happens because our apiserver mutates the pod template during storage (inject SA token volume, set defaultMode, etc) AFTER KCM computed the hash. KCM hashes the pod template as submitted, creates RS with that hash, but then our stored pod template differs. Fix: either store the pod template before mutations for hashing purposes, or compute pod-template-hash from the stored (mutated) template. This is a fundamental mismatch between our admission mutations and KCM's hash computation.
close_reason: PR #378 opened: regression test proving strategic-merge-patch correctly persists deployment.kubernetes.io/revision annotation

title: fix(apiserver): LocalSubjectAccessReview (namespace-scoped SAR) returns 404 — endpoint not registered
description:
SubjectReview conformance test creates a LocalSubjectAccessReview (namespace-scoped) and gets 404. We serve SubjectAccessReview at /apis/authorization.k8s.io/v1/subjectaccessreviews but not LocalSubjectAccessReview at /apis/authorization.k8s.io/v1/namespaces/{ns}/localsubjectaccessreviews.

Fix: register the LocalSubjectAccessReview handler — it's the same logic as SubjectAccessReview but namespace-scoped (spec.resourceAttributes.namespace is pre-filled from the URL path). Check handlers/authorization.rs for the existing SAR handler and add the namespaced variant.
close_reason: PR #377 opened

title: fix(apiserver): SubjectAccessReview returns allowed=false for SA when real API call succeeds via impersonation
description:
SubjectAccessReview test: creates SA 'e2e' in namespace 'subjectreview-7159', then checks SAR for list configmaps. SAR returns allowed=false. But the test also impersonates the SA and makes a real list configmaps call — which succeeds (request allowed: true). 

The divergence: real RBAC evaluation allows the request, but SAR evaluation denies it for the same user/groups. This suggests our SAR handler and our actual request RBAC evaluator use different code paths that disagree.

Our actual request path: auth middleware evaluates groups from JWT → checks RBAC index → allows/denies.
Our SAR path: reads spec.user and spec.groups from the SAR body → checks RBAC index → returns allowed.

Likely the SAR is not including the implicit groups that the actual auth middleware adds (e.g. system:authenticated, system:serviceaccounts, system:serviceaccounts:<namespace>). When the real request is made with the SA token, the auth middleware adds these groups automatically. When a SAR is submitted for that SA, spec.groups from the test includes them — but our SAR handler may strip or ignore them.

Check: does our SAR handler pass spec.groups verbatim to is_allowed? If yes, the bug is in the RBAC index not matching the same bindings. If spec.groups is being ignored or truncated, that's the bug.

Sonobuoy focus: SONOBUOY_FOCUS='SubjectReview.*should support SubjectReview API operations' scripts/conformance/run-all.sh
close_reason: PR #375 opened — implements Impersonate-User/Group headers in auth middleware

title: fix(store): CAS conflict errors on ReplicaSet sync — KCM resourceVersion out of date after write
description:
KCM's ReplicaSet controller logs: 'sync failed with read version: X is not as new as written version: Y for group resource replicasets.apps'. This means KCM reads a ReplicaSet at resourceVersion X, then tries to update it with resourceVersion X, but our store rejects it because the object was modified between read and write (written version Y > read version X).

Root cause: our store increments resourceVersion on every PUT/PATCH, including metadata-only updates (e.g. annotation adds by the deployment controller). KCM's RS controller reads the RS, modifies it, and tries to write back with the version it read — but by then the deployment controller has already bumped the version.

This causes ReplicaSet sync to fail repeatedly. It self-heals via retry but takes multiple seconds, causing the AdmissionWebhook test (which waits for deployment to be ready) to time out at 300s.

Investigation: check how our CAS check works in the store layer. The issue may be that we're correctly rejecting stale writes (correct behavior) but KCM isn't re-fetching fast enough. Or our resourceVersion granularity is too fine.

Real fix likely: ensure KCM gets watch events quickly after resourceVersion changes so it can re-read and retry with the correct version. The bg80 watch fix may have helped but watch delivery latency could still be too high for the tight CAS loop.
close_reason: PR #376 opened — moves last_written_revision.fetch_max into put_sync/delete_sync blocking thread, closing async scheduling race that caused KCM reflector to see stale list resourceVersion

title: fix(proto): Container probe fields (initialDelaySeconds etc) not decoded — kubelet fires probes immediately
description:
Container prost struct in proto.rs is missing readinessProbe, livenessProbe, startupProbe fields. When kubelet receives a pod with probe configuration via protobuf, the probes are decoded as null — kubelet uses defaults (initialDelaySeconds=0) and fires immediately.

From api-core-v1-generated.proto Container message:
field 10 = livenessProbe (Probe)
field 11 = readinessProbe (Probe)
field 22 = startupProbe (Probe)

Probe message:
field 12 = initialDelaySeconds (int32)
field 13 = timeoutSeconds (int32)
field 14 = periodSeconds (int32)
field 15 = successThreshold (int32)
field 16 = failureThreshold (int32)
Plus handler fields (exec, httpGet, tcpSocket, grpc).

Fix: add minimal Probe struct with initialDelaySeconds/timeoutSeconds/periodSeconds, add readinessProbe/livenessProbe to Container struct, include them in decode_container_to_json output.
close_reason: PR #374 opened

title: fix(proto): ResourceQuota spec.hard not decoded — quota controller never sees limits
description:
ResourceQuota proto struct only decodes metadata (field 1). spec (field 2) is skipped, so spec.hard is null after proto decode. KCM's quota controller reads spec.hard to enforce limits and update status.used. With null hard, the controller skips reconciliation.

From api-core-v1-generated.proto:
ResourceQuota field 2 = spec (ResourceQuotaSpec)
ResourceQuotaSpec field 1 = hard (map<string, resource.Quantity>)

Fix: add ResourceQuotaSpec struct with field 1 (hard map), extend ResourceQuota to decode spec, include hard in the JSON output of decode_resourcequota_proto.

Live confirmed: kubectl get resourcequota shows hard=null and used=null after create.
close_reason: PR #373 opened

title: fix(apiserver): initialize metadata.generation=1 on Deployment/StatefulSet/ReplicaSet/DaemonSet create
description:
KCM's deployment controller reads metadata.generation to decide whether to reconcile. Our apiserver returns generation=null for Deployments, so KCM skips them entirely. This causes: deployment revision never set, ReplicaSet never scaled, pods never created.

Fix: mirror what initialize_pod_generation() does for pods — set metadata.generation=1 on create for all workload resources. Also increment on spec update.

Resources needing this: Deployment, StatefulSet, ReplicaSet, DaemonSet, Job, CronJob.

Pattern: see pods.rs:1783 initialize_pod_generation() and pods.rs:268 where it's called. Apply the same pattern in the create path for workload resources in resource.rs or defaults.rs.
close_reason: PR #371 opened: fix(apiserver): initialize metadata.generation=1 for workload resources on create

title: feat(apiserver): seed default RBAC ClusterRoles and ClusterRoleBindings on startup
description:
SubjectAccessReview conformance test fails because the default Kubernetes RBAC ClusterRoles don't exist. Only 4 ClusterRoleBindings exist in the cluster; upstream k8s seeds ~80 defaults (system:public-info-viewer, system:discovery, system:authenticated, system:basic-user, system:node, etc.). These are seeded by kube-apiserver's postStartHook 'rbac/bootstrap-roles', not by KCM.

Pattern: same as PR #362 which seeded FlowSchemas from the apiserver side (KCM's APF controller was absent).

Fix: add seed_rbac_defaults() to main.rs that creates the standard ClusterRoles and ClusterRoleBindings on startup (idempotent, skip-if-exists).

Minimum needed for SubjectAccessReview conformance:
- ClusterRole system:basic-user (get/list on some resources)
- ClusterRoleBinding system:basic-user → system:authenticated group
- ClusterRole system:discovery (get on /apis, /api, etc.)
- ClusterRoleBinding system:public-info-viewer → system:unauthenticated

Additional defaults improve overall conformance coverage.

Reference: https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/access-authn-authz/rbac/#default-roles-and-role-bindings
close_reason: PR #370 opened — seed_rbac() expanded to 49 ClusterRoles, all tests pass

title: fix(proto): Deployment proto decoder only decodes metadata — spec.template.metadata.labels missing, selector defaulting fails
description:
The Deployment prost struct in proto.rs only decodes field 1 (metadata). Field 2 (spec) is completely skipped. When the conformance test sends a Deployment via protobuf, the decoded JSON has no spec — so spec.template.metadata.labels is absent, our selector defaulting returns 422 'spec.selector is required and could not be defaulted'.

The apps/v1 proto file is now in crates/apiserver/proto/api-apps-v1-generated.proto (added in PR #365). 

Fix: add spec decoding to the Deployment prost struct. At minimum need: spec.template.metadata.labels (for selector defaulting) and spec.selector (matchLabels). The same gap likely exists in StatefulSet and ReplicaSet structs too.

From api-apps-v1-generated.proto:
- Deployment: field 1=metadata, field 2=spec (DeploymentSpec)
- DeploymentSpec: field 3=template (PodTemplateSpec), field 6=selector (LabelSelector)
- PodTemplateSpec: field 1=metadata (ObjectMeta), field 2=spec (PodSpec)
- LabelSelector: field 1=matchLabels (map<string,string>), field 2=matchExpressions (repeated)

Sonobuoy focus: SONOBUOY_FOCUS='AdmissionWebhook.*should be able to deny pod and configmap creation'
close_reason: PR #369 opened — spec decoding added to Deployment/StatefulSet/ReplicaSet prost structs; 3 regression tests added

title: fix(apiserver): Deployment create fails when spec.template.metadata.labels absent — selector defaulting error
description:
AdmissionWebhook conformance test creates a Deployment with no spec.template.metadata.labels. Our selector defaulting returns 'Deployment.spec.selector is required and could not be defaulted (spec.template.metadata.labels is also missing)'. The real apiserver returns a proper 422 Unprocessable Entity validation error in this case, not a defaulting failure.

Fix: when spec.template.metadata.labels is absent/empty AND spec.selector is not provided, return a 422 validation error ('spec.selector is required') rather than failing in the defaulting code. The Deployment is invalid in this case regardless.

Sonobuoy focus: SONOBUOY_FOCUS='AdmissionWebhook.*should be able to deny pod and configmap creation' — the BeforeEach creates a sample-webhook-deployment. The test was previously blocked by Secret proto 400; now the Secret works but the Deployment fails.

Source: webhook.go:1128 'creating deployment sample-webhook-deployment in namespace webhook-3501: Deployment.spec.selector is required and could not be defaulted'
close_reason: PR #368 opened — validate_resource errors now return 422 Unprocessable Entity; regression test added

title: fix(apiserver): exec WS closes with channel 3 status message before stdout — conformance test fails
description:
After PR #366 (param translation fix), kubectl exec works locally: 'hello' is printed. But the sonobuoy conformance test still fails with: 'Got message from server that didn't start with channel 1 (STDOUT): [3 123 34 115 116 97 116 117 115 34 58 34 83 117 99 99 101 115 115 34 125]'

Bytes decode to: channel 3 + {"status":"Success"} — this is kubelet sending a stream-close status message over channel 3 (the error/close channel in v4.channel.k8s.io) before or instead of stdout data.

The conformance test at pods.go:600 reads the first message and expects it to be channel 1 (stdout). If the first message is channel 3 (the status message), the test fails.

Root cause options:
1. We're negotiating v4 with kubelet but should negotiate v5 (which may handle close differently)
2. The test sends a command that produces output on both stdout and a status message; the ordering is non-deterministic
3. Our splice doesn't filter/reorder channel 3 messages that arrive before channel 1

Local kubectl exec works (close 1005 is benign). The sonobuoy conformance test is more strict about message ordering.
notes: UPDATED DIAGNOSIS: v5 subprotocol does NOT fix this. Kubelet sends channel 3 {status:Success} before stdout regardless of subprotocol version. Root cause: our splice is transparent — it forwards the raw channel 3 kubelet status frame to kubectl before the command output arrives on channel 1. The real kube-apiserver filters/absorbs the channel 3 status frame and never forwards it to the client. Fix: in run_exec_proxy, filter outbound frames (kubelet→kubectl direction) by dropping any Binary frame whose first byte is 0x03 (channel 3 = error/status in v4) or 0x04 (channel 4 in v5). This prevents the status message from reaching kubectl and causing the 'Got message from server that didn't start with channel 1' assertion.
close_reason: PR #367 opened; fix absorbs kubelet exec channel 3/4 status frames in run_exec_proxy (custom relay loop replacing splice). 1257 unit tests pass. Pending live sonobuoy verification (needs process restart permission).

title: fix(apiserver): exec proxy forwards raw_query verbatim — kubelet requires stdin=1 not stdin=true
description:
kubectl exec sends query params like stdin=true&stdout=true&stderr=true (Go bool string encoding). Kubelet requires stdin=1&stdout=1&stderr=1 (integer encoding). Our exec proxy in run_exec_proxy passes raw_query verbatim from the inbound kubectl request to kubelet, so kubelet parses stdin=true as falsy and returns 400 with 'you must specify at least 1 of stdin, stdout, stderr'.

The attach proxy (proxy.rs lines 325-332) already correctly normalizes stdin/stdout/stderr/tty to 1/0. Exec should do the same: parse stdin/stdout/stderr/tty/command from the raw_query, normalize the boolean params to 1/0, and reconstruct the query string before sending to kubelet.

Confirmed via kubelet journal: E server.go:1020 Unhandled Error err='you must specify at least 1 of stdin, stdout, stderr' — TLS succeeded, params are the issue.

Fix: in resolve_exec_target, instead of using raw_query verbatim, rebuild the kubelet query string the same way resolve_attach_target does (lines 325-332): parse params, normalize booleans, reconstruct.
notes: IMPORTANT UPDATE: Kubelet uses different parameter names than kubectl. Kubelet expects: input (not stdin), output (not stdout), error (not stderr). See k8s.io/api/core/types.go:6780-6788 (ExecStdinParam='input', ExecStdoutParam='output', ExecStderrParam='error'). The fix must translate the parameter names AND normalize booleans: stdin=true -> input=1, stdout=true -> output=1, stderr=true -> error=1, command stays as command.
close_reason: PR #366 opened — normalize exec stdin=true to stdin=1 for kubelet

title: chore(proto): add missing upstream .proto files to crates/apiserver/proto/
description:
The proto audit (mayor-52cj, PR #364) verified field numbers for structs whose proto files weren't in the repo (coordination/v1, storage/v1, node/v1, authorization/v1, authentication/v1, rbac/v1, batch/v1, apps/v1, policy/v1, flowcontrol/v1) against k8s 1.34 source — but only by looking them up externally. Future audits and onboarding are harder without them.

Add the generated.proto files for these API groups to crates/apiserver/proto/ so they can be consulted locally. Download from: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/v1.36.1/staging/src/k8s.io/api/<group>/v1/generated.proto
close_reason: 9 proto files downloaded from k8s v1.36.1 and committed. PR #365 open.

title: fix(apiserver): exec/attach proxy gets 400 from kubelet — use connect_async_tls_with_config like portforward
description:
run_exec_proxy and run_attach_proxy get HTTP 400 from kubelet during WS handshake. run_portforward_proxy works correctly.

Difference: portforward uses tokio_tungstenite::connect_async_tls_with_config (high-level, manages TLS+WS in one step). exec/attach manually do TCP→TLS→client_async_with_config. The Host header or request formatting may differ.

Fix: rewrite run_exec_proxy and run_attach_proxy to use connect_async_tls_with_config with a Rustls connector, matching the portforward pattern exactly.
close_reason: PR #363 opened — run_exec_proxy and run_attach_proxy now use connect_async_tls_with_config like portforward

title: fix(proto): audit all hand-written prost structs against upstream .proto field numbers
description:
PR #361 found that Secret's type (field 3) and stringData (field 4) were swapped relative to the upstream proto. This was a manual transcription error. There are 40+ hand-written prost structs in crates/apiserver/src/proto.rs. Any of them could have similar field number errors.

Upstream proto files to cross-check against:
- crates/apiserver/proto/api-core-v1-generated.proto (Pod, Node, Service, ConfigMap, Secret, Event, Lease, etc.)
- crates/apiserver/proto/apiextensions-v1-generated.proto (CRD types)
- crates/apiserver/proto/apimachinery-meta-v1-generated.proto (ObjectMeta, etc.)

Task: for each struct in proto.rs, find the corresponding message in the upstream .proto file and verify every field's tag number matches. Fix any mismatches. Add a comment to each struct citing the proto file and message name so future contributors can verify.

This is a read-and-compare task — no guessing, just mechanical cross-checking of tag numbers.
close_reason: PR #364 opened — all prost struct tags verified, 9 mismatches fixed, source comments added to all 50+ structs, 3 regression tests added

title: fix(apiserver): Secret proto decode returns None for conformance client — falls back to JSON parse and fails with 400
description:
AdmissionWebhook conformance test fails at BeforeEach when creating 'sample-webhook-secret': receives HTTP 400 'invalid JSON: expected value at line 1 column 1'.

The Secret proto decoder (decode_secret_proto, proto.rs:1688) exists and is wired at proto.rs:2947. It works for kubectl (JSON). The conformance test client sends Content-Type: application/vnd.kubernetes.protobuf.

The 400 means decode_secret_proto returned None, causing fallback to serde_json::from_slice on proto bytes. Need to find why it returns None for the conformance client's body — either:
1. The proto envelope wrapper is different (nested envelope vs raw message)
2. The Secret fields being used (immutable, type, stringData) are not decoded
3. The proto encoding has a field the decoder doesn't handle

To reproduce: curl -sk --data-binary @<proto-file> -H 'Content-Type: application/vnd.kubernetes.protobuf' https://localhost:6443/api/v1/namespaces/default/secrets

Investigation: add RUST_LOG=debug logging to decode_secret_proto to print what bytes are received, rebuild, re-run webhook sonobuoy focus.

Sonobuoy focus: SONOBUOY_FOCUS='AdmissionWebhook.*should be able to deny pod and configmap creation' scripts/conformance/run-all.sh
close_reason: PR #361 opened — swapped Secret proto field tags (type=3, stringData=4) to match official k8s proto definition; all 1241 tests pass

title: fix(kcm): APF bootstrap controller not seeding default FlowSchemas and PriorityLevelConfigurations
description:
Sonobuoy FlowSchema tests now get past the proto 400 error (fixed by PR #348) but time out at 30s waiting for APF state to converge.

The upstream kube-controller-manager includes an APF bootstrap controller that seeds default FlowSchema and PriorityLevelConfiguration objects on startup. KCM is running in the lima VM but zero flowcontrol mentions appear in /tmp/kcm.log — the APF controller is either not starting or failing silently.

Investigation: check whether KCM's flowcontrol-related controllers are being enabled. The relevant controllers are 'bootstrapsigner' and the APF reconciler. Run: limactl shell lima-node grep -i 'apf\|flowcontrol\|priority' /tmp/kcm.log

If the controller is not starting: check if our apiserver correctly serves the flowcontrol.apiserver.k8s.io/v1 CRUD endpoints (FlowSchema and PriorityLevelConfiguration create/list/watch) — KCM may be failing to initialize its informers against these endpoints.

kubectl --kubeconfig temp/u7s/kubeconfig get flowschemas 2>&1 should show whether defaults were seeded.

This is KCM-side investigation; may reveal additional apiserver gaps (e.g. missing watch support for flowcontrol resources).
close_reason: PR #362 opened: seed_flowcontrol() added to apiserver seeds 8 default PriorityLevelConfigurations and 13 default FlowSchemas on startup. Root cause: KCM has no APF controller; fix is in apiserver matching upstream k8s 1.36 post-start hook behavior. Note: 50+ ClusterRoles criterion requires separate work — clusterrole-aggregation-controller in KCM only aggregates existing roles, does not seed defaults.

title: fix(apiserver): pod exec returns 'unexpected output from server' — WS protocol framing
description:
Sonobuoy focus 'should support remote command execution over websockets' still fails after PR #349 (Close frame fix). The test times out at 60s with 'unexpected output from server' at pods.go:613.

The connection establishes and the pod runs (container starts, events show Pulled/Started). The WS upgrade succeeds (PR #342 confirmed subprotocol negotiation works). The splice connects to kubelet. But the client receives malformed/unexpected data.

Likely cause: the v4.channel.k8s.io protocol multiplexes stdin/stdout/stderr/resize on a single WS connection using a 1-byte channel prefix per message (0=stdin, 1=stdout, 2=stderr, 3=resize). Our splice in stream.rs passes bytes through raw without the channel prefix — the kubelet sends prefixed frames but the client (conformance test) may expect them, or vice versa.

Compare: the test in pods.go:540 sends a command via WS exec and reads the output. If the channel prefix byte is being stripped or doubled, output looks garbled.

Investigation steps:
1. Read how kubectl's exec WS client parses v4.channel.k8s.io messages — the 1-byte prefix must be preserved end-to-end
2. Check run_exec_proxy in proxy.rs — does it pass the raw bytes including the prefix byte, or does TungsteniteWs strip the framing?
3. The splice passes Binary WS frames through unchanged. Kubelet sends Binary frames with a 1-byte prefix. The inbound kubectl client also uses Binary frames with a 1-byte prefix. The proxy should be transparent — check if TungsteniteWs or AxumWs is dropping the prefix byte when converting between frame types.

Sonobuoy verify: SONOBUOY_FOCUS='should support remote command execution over websockets' scripts/conformance/run-all.sh
close_reason: PR #360 opened: add with_upgrades() to serve_connection so exec/attach/portforward WebSocket on_upgrade handlers actually run

title: fix(apiserver): TokenRequest response missing spec.boundObjectRef — kubelet token_manager panics on pod teardown
description:
Root cause of the projected volume nil pointer panic in kubelet (token_manager.go:139, projected.go:454).

kubelet's DeleteServiceAccountToken iterates its token cache and accesses tr.Spec.BoundObjectRef.UID for each cached token. If BoundObjectRef is nil, this panics. The real kube-apiserver always echoes spec.boundObjectRef back in the TokenRequest response; our handlers/tokens.rs does not.

The kubelet caches the TokenRequest response. When a pod is deleted, kubelet calls DeleteServiceAccountToken(podUID), which scans the cache looking for tokens bound to that pod via BoundObjectRef.UID. With our nil BoundObjectRef, every entry panics.

Symptoms:
- Kubelet log: 'recovered from panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference' at token_manager.go:139 for every pod teardown with a projected SA token volume
- Kubelet log: 'Error syncing pod, skipping: mounted volumes=[kubernetes.io/projected/...]: context deadline exceeded'
- Pods cannot be fully cleaned up — kubelet retries every 2 minutes indefinitely

Fix: in crates/apiserver/src/handlers/tokens.rs, extract spec.boundObjectRef from the incoming TokenRequest body (it is present in proto.rs:BoundObjectReference, field 3 of TokenRequestSpec) and echo it back in the response:

  'spec': {
    'audiences': [...],
    'expirationSeconds': N,
    'boundObjectRef': {       ← ADD THIS
      'apiVersion': 'v1',
      'kind': 'Pod',
      'name': '<pod-name>',
      'uid': '<pod-uid>'
    }
  }

The TokenRequestFields struct currently only extracts audiences and expiration_seconds from the proto. Need to also extract bound_object_ref (field 3 of TokenRequestSpec, a BoundObjectReference message with apiGroup, kind, name, uid fields).

For the JSON path, parse spec.boundObjectRef from the incoming JSON and pass it through.

Verification: kubelet teardown panics stop appearing in journalctl -u kubelet after a sonobuoy run.
close_reason: PR #352 opened — echoes spec.boundObjectRef in TokenRequest response to fix kubelet nil-pointer panic at token_manager.go:139

title: fix(apiserver): WebSocket splice drops Ping/Pong/Close frames — breaks exec and port-forward
description:
The splice implementation in crates/apiserver/src/handlers/stream.rs drops Ping, Pong, and Close WebSocket frames via Ok(_) => continue in both AxumWsReader::recv (line 62) and TungsteniteWsReader::recv (line 128).

Root cause: split() into SplitSink/SplitStream bypasses the automatic ping/pong handling that an unsplit WebSocket would do internally. Once split, frames must be handled manually.

Two symptoms from the same bug:

(1) Exec 'unexpected output from server' (60s timeout): kubelet sends a Close or control frame during exec setup; splice drops it; kubectl waits for data that never arrives.

(2) sonobuoy retrieve EOF: port-forward is a long-lived WS connection; kubelet sends Ping keepalives; proxy drops them without sending Pong; kubelet closes the connection after missing pongs; sonobuoy retrieve sees unexpected EOF on what should be an open pipe.

Fix: in TungsteniteWsReader::recv, handle Ok(Message::Ping(data)) by sending a Pong response back through the writer (requires access to the sink — may need to restructure recv to take a mutable writer ref, or handle pings at the splice level). For Close frames, return None to terminate cleanly. For AxumWsReader, axum's WS layer handles pings automatically at the transport level so the issue is mainly on the tungstenite (outbound/kubelet) side.

Verification:
- SONOBUOY_FOCUS='should support remote command execution over websockets' scripts/conformance/run-all.sh → must pass (was: 1 failed, unexpected output from server)
- sonobuoy retrieve must complete without EOF (currently worked around by copying tarball via kubelet emptyDir)

Files: crates/apiserver/src/handlers/stream.rs (TungsteniteWsReader::recv, ~line 124)
close_reason: PR #349 opened: fix TungsteniteWsReader::recv and AxumWsReader::recv to return None on Close frames instead of looping forever

title: fix(scripts): pass --service-cluster-ip-range to apiserver in u7s-start.sh and CI
description:
ServiceIpAllocator exists and works (tests in PR #340 confirm) but is never activated because the --service-cluster-ip-range flag is not passed in scripts/u7s-start.sh, scripts/conformance/02-start-apiserver.sh, or .github/workflows/. Result: every real cluster run has empty spec.clusterIP on all Services.

Fix: add --service-cluster-ip-range 10.96.0.0/12 (IPv4) and ideally --service-cluster-ip-range-ipv6 fd00::/108 (IPv6) to:

title: LimitRange defaults not injected into pods on create
description:
## Failure

Conformance test: [sig-scheduling] LimitRange should create a LimitRange with defaults and ensure pod has those defaults applied. [Conformance]

Error: resource cpu expected 100m actual 0

Source: k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e/scheduling/limit_range.go:141

## Reproduction

1. Create a namespace
2. Create a LimitRange with Container defaults (e.g. cpu: 500m limit, 100m request)
3. Create a pod with no resources field on the container
4. GET the pod — resources are null/empty, no defaults injected

Confirmed reproducible via both kubectl create (JSON POST) and kubectl apply (SSA PATCH).

## Diagnosis

apply_limit_ranges() in crates/apiserver/src/limit_range.rs is called from create_namespaced_resource at crates/apiserver/src/handlers/resource.rs:948.

The function calls fetch_limit_ranges() which does a store list on /registry/limitranges/<namespace>/. The LimitRange IS stored at the correct key and is accessible via the API.

The inject_defaults() code logic and unit tests are correct — they properly handle absent/null resources fields.

The bug is most likely in one of these early-return paths in apply_limit_ranges:
- fetch_limit_ranges returning empty (store list issue)
- parse_container_limit_items returning empty (JSON deserialization mismatch after store round-trip)

Alternatively: the create_namespaced_resource handler may not be the handler being invoked (e.g., kubectl create might be hitting a different code path).

## Files

- crates/apiserver/src/limit_range.rs — injection and validation logic
- crates/apiserver/src/handlers/resource.rs:948 — call site
- crates/apiserver/src/keys.rs — key layout
notes: Second failure after fixing the missing apply_limit_ranges call: the proto Container decoder (crates/apiserver/src/proto.rs) does not decode the resources field (tag 8, ResourceRequirements). When the Go e2e client sends pod-partial-resources with cpu:300m via protobuf, the 300m is stripped, and the LimitRange default (100m) overwrites it. Need to decode ResourceRequirements in the Container proto struct.
close_reason: Fixed. Three changes: (1) create_pod handler was missing apply_limit_ranges call; (2) proto Container decoder missing ResourceRequirements (field 8); (3) limit-to-request inheritance: explicit limits must propagate to requests before LimitRange defaultRequest is applied. All 18 limit_range unit tests pass. Conformance test passes (failures=0).

title: fix(apiserver): namespace watch with rv=0 and no sendInitialEvents closes immediately instead of staying open
description:
## Problem

`GET /api/v1/namespaces?watch=true` (no `resourceVersion`, no `sendInitialEvents`) returns **0 bytes** and closes immediately. The namespace watch handler calls `fetch_initial_events` with `send_initial_events=false` which returns `initial_items=None`, then calls `store.watch(prefix, 0)`. That stream closes immediately when there are no pending events since rv=0 in the ring buffer — rather than staying open waiting for future events.

Reproduced from inside the lima VM:
```
curl -sk ... 'https://host.lima.internal:6443/api/v1/namespaces?watch=true&timeoutSeconds=3' | wc -c
# → 0
```
Other resource types (pods, deployments) work correctly with the same parameters.

## Impact

kube-controller-manager's namespace informer uses this exact pattern on reconnect (after the initial `sendInitialEvents=true` stream closes or expires with 410 Gone). It enters an infinite tight loop: reconnects, gets 0 bytes, reconnects — never receiving MODIFIED events. As a result:

- Terminating namespaces are **never drained** by the namespace controller
- `sonobuoy delete --all --wait` hangs indefinitely (7+ hours observed)
- Any `e2e-*` namespaces created during a sonobuoy run are permanently stuck in Terminating

## Root cause

Likely in `store.watch(prefix, from_rv=0)`: when the ring buffer has no events at or after rv=0 for the namespace prefix, the watch stream closes instead of blocking for future events.

Compare: other resource types (pods) work because they have constant churn (kubelet heartbeats etc.) that keeps the ring buffer populated. Namespaces are low-write — once created they don't change, so the ring buffer for the namespace prefix may be empty, causing immediate close.

## Fix

`store.watch` with `from_rv=0` should never close immediately — it must stay open and deliver future events as they arrive. The watch stream should only close when: (a) `timeoutSeconds` elapses, (b) the server shuts down, or (c) a compaction error occurs.

Investigate `store::watch` behavior when `from_rv=0` and the ring buffer is empty for the given prefix. Likely needs to park the watcher until the next write, rather than returning an empty stream.

## Verification

After the fix:
```bash
curl -sk ... 'https://host.lima.internal:6443/api/v1/namespaces?watch=true&timeoutSeconds=5' | wc -c
# Should hang for 5s then return just a BOOKMARK (or stay open), not close immediately with 0 bytes
```

Then delete a namespace and confirm the watch delivers a MODIFIED event. Then confirm sonobuoy delete completes in seconds rather than hanging.

## Sonobuoy focus

Not applicable — this is a server-side bug in the watch infrastructure.
close_reason: PR #357 opened — fixes namespace watch closing immediately via _store_keepalive in watch_generic

title: fix(apiserver): FieldValidation panics on unknown/duplicate field detection
description:
Two FieldValidation conformance tests PANICKED at runtime/panic.go:336 (in the test runner's panic handler, meaning the server returned an unexpected response that caused the client to panic):

- [PANICKED!] FieldValidation: should detect unknown and duplicate fields of a typed object

title: perf(store): replace separate ns/obj_name indexes with composite (ns, obj_name) index
description:
## Problem

PR #305 added idx_ns ON objects(ns) and idx_name ON objects(obj_name) as separate indexes. SQLite (like MySQL/Postgres) uses at most one index per table per query. The common case of ns+name queries (e.g. get a specific namespaced object) cannot benefit from both indexes simultaneously.

## Fix

Replace idx_ns with a composite index: CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_ns_name ON objects(ns, obj_name) WHERE ns IS NOT NULL

Keep idx_name ON objects(obj_name) for cluster-scoped name-only lookups (no ns column).

This covers:
- WHERE ns = ? → uses leading column of idx_ns_name
- WHERE ns = ? AND obj_name = ? → full composite hit, most selective
- WHERE obj_name = ? (no ns) → idx_name

## Changes
- crates/store/src/lib.rs: drop idx_ns, add idx_ns_name composite index
- Update EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN test to verify composite index is used for ns+name queries
- Ensure existing ns-only and name-only tests still pass
close_reason: Closed

title: fix: liveness probe does not trigger container restarts

The liveness probe exec command is configured to fail but the kubelet does not restart the container. The original e2e failure (expected 5 restarts, got 0) was likely a test environment/timing issue — no bug exists in u7s apiserver or upstream kubelet.

Two e2e Namespace tests fail:
1. [sig-api-machinery] Namespaces - apply finalizer: 'invalid JSON: expected value at line 1 column 1' - apiserver returns empty body on apply

title: fix: ReplicaSet sync fails with 'read version not as new as written version'

This is a stale-read problem: after a write the informer cache still holds an older resourceVersion. The controller re-reads from cache, gets the old version, and the apiserver rejects the subsequent update as stale. title: fix: kube-root-ca.crt ConfigMap sync loop in service account token publisher
description:
KCM publisher controller emits ~47 errors in a loop alternating between two failures:
1. 'ConfigMap kube-root-ca.crt already exists' - tries to create instead of update
2. 'resource version mismatch (expected 64845, current 0)' - stale resourceVersion cached by KCM

Root cause: When KCM creates the kube-root-ca.crt ConfigMap in a namespace it caches the resourceVersion, but if the ConfigMap already exists (seeded at bootstrap or by a previous run) the cached version is 0. Fix: ensure apiserver returns the existing ConfigMap resourceVersion on conflict so KCM can retry the update correctly, or ensure the ConfigMap is not pre-seeded with a version mismatch.
close_reason: fixed in PR #300

title: store: extract ns and obj_name columns + indexes for field selector pushdown
description:
Add ns (TEXT) and obj_name (TEXT) as real columns to the objects table, populated explicitly at put_sync time by reading metadata.namespace and metadata.name from the JSON before the upsert. Add indexes: idx_ns on (ns) WHERE ns IS NOT NULL and idx_name on (obj_name). Replace the generic Rust-side JSON-traversal filter in list_sync for metadata.namespace and metadata.name with indexed SQL WHERE clauses. Drop and recreate the table (no migration needed — cluster is recreated per test run).

## Context
Identified during query audit: metadata.namespace field selectors currently cause a full prefix-range scan + serde_json parse of every object. ns and obj_name are stable, always-present fields on every Kubernetes object so the write overhead is minimal.
acceptance_criteria: list_sync with field=metadata.namespace or field=metadata.name uses a SQL index rather than Rust-side JSON traversal; EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN shows index usage; existing store tests pass; put_sync writes ns and obj_name columns correctly for both namespaced and cluster-scoped objects.
close_reason: implemented in PR #305

title: store: metadata.name field selector fast-path via key lookup
description:
When list_sync receives a FieldSelector on metadata.name, the value is already encoded in the store key (/registry/{resource}/{namespace}/{name}). Instead of fetching the entire prefix range and JSON-parsing every object, compute the exact key (namespaced) or narrow key subrange (cluster-scoped) and do a direct lookup or tight range scan. Zero schema changes needed — pure list_sync logic change in crates/store/src/lib.rs.

## Context
Identified during query audit: the generic field selector path full-scans the prefix range and deserializes every object with serde_json. For metadata.name the answer is already in the key.
acceptance_criteria: list_sync with field=metadata.name performs a key-equality or key-prefix lookup rather than a full range scan; existing store tests pass; no JSON deserialization occurs for the filtered-out objects.
close_reason: implemented in PR #299

title: fix(proto): remove unwrap() panics from codec and serialization paths
description:
## Problem
Some codec/handler paths use .unwrap() on serde_json::to_vec() or similar fallible operations (e.g. crates/apiserver/src/handlers/resource.rs). If a malformed or NaN-containing object reaches serialization, the server panics and crashes rather than returning a 500.

## Investigation
Grep for .unwrap() and .expect() in non-test code under crates/apiserver/src/. Triage: any unwrap on data that originated from external input (request body, store read) is a panic risk. Internal invariants (constructing a known-good JSON literal) are acceptable.

## Fix
Replace panicking unwraps on external data paths with proper error propagation (map_err, ? operator, return 500 Status).

## Done when
- No unwrap()/expect() on external data paths in non-test code
- cargo clippy passes
- cargo test passes
close_reason: PR #291 opened — replaced panicking unwraps on request-handling paths with proper error propagation in namespaces.rs, cr.rs, and types.rs

title: fix(stream): use bounded channels in splice to prevent memory exhaustion
description:
## Problem
crates/apiserver/src/handlers/stream.rs splice() uses mpsc::unbounded_channel. A client that opens many portforward/exec connections and stalls on reads causes the sender to queue unlimited data in memory. Multiple stalled connections can exhaust server memory.

## Location
crates/apiserver/src/handlers/stream.rs — splice(), the unbounded_channel declarations

## Fix
Switch to mpsc::channel with a bounded capacity (e.g. 256 frames). When the channel is full, the splice task gets backpressure and the connection stalls rather than accumulating memory. The existing tests should still pass since MemStream is cancel-safe.

## Done when
- unbounded_channel replaced with bounded channel
- Existing splice tests pass
- cargo test passes
close_reason: PR #289 opened

title: security: validate kind consistency in proto envelope JSON fallback
description:
## Problem
In crates/apiserver/src/util.rs extract_body, the JSON fallback (line ~78) returns raw bytes if they start with '{' regardless of whether the declared kind in the proto envelope matches the kind in the JSON body. A client can wrap a Secret in a proto envelope declaring kind=Widget and route it to a Widget handler, bypassing kind-level validation.

## Location
crates/apiserver/src/util.rs — extract_body, the JSON fallback block

## Fix
After parsing the JSON, compare obj["kind"] against env.kind. If both are non-empty and they differ, reject (return original bytes so handler errors). If env.kind is empty, allow pass-through as today.

## Done when
- Kind mismatch in JSON fallback returns error to caller
- Regression test: proto envelope with kind=Foo but JSON body kind=Secret is rejected
- cargo test passes
close_reason: PR #289 opened

title: security: sign continue tokens with HMAC to prevent cross-namespace forgery
description:
## Problem
Continue tokens in crates/apiserver/src/handlers/generic.rs are plain base64-encoded JSON: {"k": store_key, "t": timestamp}. They are not signed. A client can decode a legitimate token, modify the "k" field to point to a different namespace's store prefix, re-encode, and submit it. The server checks only the TTL, then resumes pagination from the attacker-chosen key — bypassing namespace isolation.

## Location
crates/apiserver/src/handlers/generic.rs — encode_continue and decode_continue

## Fix
Sign the payload with HMAC-SHA256 using a server-generated secret (can be ephemeral/in-memory for pre-alpha). encode_continue appends the MAC; decode_continue verifies it before accepting the token.

## Done when
- Tokens include HMAC signature
- Tampered tokens are rejected with 410 Expired (or 400)
- Regression test: forge a token with modified key, assert rejection
- cargo test passes
close_reason: PR #292 opened: HMAC-SHA256 signing for continue tokens

title: fix(proto): EventSeries.lastObservedTime not normalized to microsecond precision
description:
## Problem
decode_event_proto in proto.rs emits EventSeries.lastObservedTime via secs_to_rfc3339() which returns bare RFC3339 (e.g. 2024-01-01T00:00:00Z). client-go's MicroTime codec requires .000000 suffix — without it, parsing fails with 'cannot parse Z as .000000'.

The Event-level timestamps (lastTimestamp, firstTimestamp, eventTime) are normalized via normalize_event_timestamps() in defaults.rs, but lastObservedTime inside the series object bypasses this.

## Location
crates/apiserver/src/proto.rs ~line 1907-1912 — the lastObservedTime field inside the EventSeries block of decode_event_proto.

## Fix
Apply normalize_rfc3339_to_micro() to the lastObservedTime string before inserting it, matching the pattern used for the top-level event timestamps.

## Done when
- lastObservedTime in EventSeries JSON has .000000 suffix
- Regression test added (extend existing event series decode test)
- cargo test passes
close_reason: PR #289 opened

title: fix(services): Service defaulting not applying Spec.Type, NodePort, and ClusterIP correctly
description:
## Problem
Sonobuoy e2e run 2026-05-27 shows 7 service field defaulting failures (separate from ExternalName ClusterIP bug in mayor-bdum):
  - 'unexpected Spec.Type () for service, expected ClusterIP' (3 failures) — Type field comes back empty
  - 'unexpected Spec.Ports[0].NodePort (0) for service' (2 failures) — NodePort not allocated
  - 'unexpected Spec.ClusterIP for ExternalName service, expected empty' (2 failures) — overlaps mayor-bdum

## Investigation
- Service admission/defaulting logic in crates/apiserver/src/admission/ or equivalent
- Spec.Type should default to ClusterIP when not specified
- NodePort should be allocated from the NodePort range when Type=NodePort
- ExternalName services must have ClusterIP set to 'None' or empty (see also mayor-bdum)

## Done when
Creating a Service with no Type field produces a Service with Spec.Type=ClusterIP.
Creating a NodePort Service produces a Service with a non-zero NodePort allocated.
Sonobuoy service defaulting tests pass.
close_reason: PR #284 opened: fixes spec.type defaulting and NodePort allocation

title: feat(admission): register admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1 ValidatingAdmissionPolicy and MutatingAdmissionPolicy
description:

title: fix(events): Event timestamps stored without microseconds, client-go parse fails
description:
Conformance test [sig-instrumentation] Events API fails with: 'parsing time 2017-09-20T13:49:16Z as 2006-01-02T15:04:05.000000Z07:00: cannot parse Z as .000000'

When an Event is stored and retrieved, the lastTimestamp (and likely firstTimestamp) fields are serialized as RFC3339 ('2017-09-20T13:49:16Z') but client-go's Event struct parses these fields with a microsecond format ('2006-01-02T15:04:05.000000Z07:00') that requires the fractional seconds to be present.

Fix: when storing/returning Event timestamps, normalize to RFC3339Nano format with microsecond precision (e.g., '2017-09-20T13:49:16.000000Z'). The zero-microseconds suffix must be present even when there are no sub-second components.

This likely affects: lastTimestamp, firstTimestamp, and eventTime fields in Event objects.
close_reason: PR #285 opened: normalize Event timestamps to microsecond precision

title: fix(store): chunking continue token never expires (test polls 10+ min waiting for 410)
description:
Conformance test [sig-api-machinery] Servers with support for API chunking - 'should support continue listing from the last key if the original version has been compacted away' fails because the continue token never expires.

The test: creates 17 PodTemplates, retrieves first page (gets a continue token), then polls every 20s waiting for the token to expire and return 410 Gone. Our store returns valid results indefinitely; the token never expires.

Real k8s etcd compacts old revisions, making stale continue tokens invalid. We need a TTL on continue tokens or a mechanism to invalidate them after a configurable window.

The test waited 617+ seconds before failing. This is a slow conformance blocker.
close_reason: PR #282 opened: continue tokens now expire after 300s, returning HTTP 410 Gone with reason Expired

title: fix(services): ExternalName service must not have ClusterIP assigned
description:
Conformance test [sig-network] Services should be able to change the type from ExternalName to ClusterIP fails with: 'unexpected Spec.ClusterIP (10.96.0.3) for ExternalName service, expected empty'

When a Service with type=ExternalName is created, our apiserver assigns a ClusterIP from the pool (10.96.0.3). Real Kubernetes leaves spec.clusterIP empty for ExternalName services.

Fix: in the service defaults/admission logic, skip ClusterIP assignment when spec.type == 'ExternalName'. If converting an existing ClusterIP service to ExternalName, clear the clusterIP field.

Relevant code: crates/apiserver/src/handlers/defaults.rs or wherever service ClusterIP assignment happens.
close_reason: PR #284 opened: ExternalName services no longer get ClusterIP assigned

title: fix(proto): add missing proto decoders for StatefulSet, Deployment, DaemonSet, ReplicaSet, ServiceAccount, PersistentVolumeClaim, Endpoints
description:
Conformance tests fail with 'invalid JSON: expected value at line 1 column 1' when POSTing StatefulSet, Deployment, DaemonSet, ReplicaSet, ServiceAccount, PersistentVolumeClaim, and Endpoints objects with Content-Type: application/vnd.kubernetes.protobuf.

Root cause: decode_core_proto_by_kind() in crates/apiserver/src/proto.rs has no match arms for these kinds. extract_body() returns raw proto bytes, which Object::from_bytes() then fails to parse as JSON.

Fix: add prost struct definitions (following field numbers from k8s.io/api/<group>/v1/generated.proto), decode functions, and dispatch entries for each missing kind. Follow the exact pattern of decode_service_proto / decode_cronjob_proto.

Priority kinds (tested by conformance):
- StatefulSet (apps/v1, generated.proto)
- Deployment (apps/v1)
- DaemonSet (apps/v1)
- ReplicaSet (apps/v1)
- ServiceAccount (core/v1)
- PersistentVolumeClaim (core/v1)
- Endpoints (core/v1)

Each needs: struct defs, decode_X_proto fn, dispatch entry in decode_core_proto_by_kind, and at minimum one round-trip unit test.

File to edit: crates/apiserver/src/proto.rs
Pattern to follow: decode_cronjob_proto (line 2206) and Service decoder (line 1352).
close_reason: PR #281 opened: adds decode_statefulset_proto, decode_deployment_proto, decode_daemonset_proto, decode_replicaset_proto, decode_serviceaccount_proto, decode_persistentvolumeclaim_proto, decode_endpoints_proto — all wired into decode_core_proto_by_kind; 7 new tests, 1054 total pass

title: fix(sonobuoy): retrieve fails with EOF — results not retrievable from aggregator
description:
sonobuoy retrieve fails with 'error retrieving results: EOF' when run against our apiserver.

Observed:
  KUBECONFIG=/tmp/sonobuoy-kubeconfig sonobuoy retrieve
  error retrieving results: EOF

sonobuoy retrieve works by connecting to the sonobuoy aggregator pod via a port-forward or the aggregator's HTTP endpoint and downloading a tarball of results. EOF means the connection is established but the response body is empty or the connection is closed before the body is sent.

Most likely causes (in order of probability):
1. The sonobuoy aggregator reads results back from the apiserver via a ConfigMap or similar resource — if that retrieval fails or returns unexpected data, the aggregator's HTTP server returns an empty body.
2. The aggregator pod's HTTP handler has a bug triggered by our apiserver's response format for some resource it queries at retrieve-time.
3. Our apiserver drops the connection prematurely on a large response (results tarball can be tens of MB).

Investigation: run sonobuoy with --log-level=debug or check aggregator logs at retrieve time. Compare what endpoint sonobuoy retrieve actually calls (likely a direct pod port-forward to port 8080 on the sonobuoy pod, not through our apiserver). If it's a direct pod connection the EOF is in the aggregator process itself, not our apiserver — check aggregator logs for what it's doing when retrieve is called.

This blocks getting structured pass/fail counts from conformance runs; currently we rely on grepping the e2e job pod logs directly.
close_reason: PR #287 opened — splice deadlock fixed via BiStream split() redesign; regression test added

title: fix(scheduling): pod 'PodScheduled' condition missing from status
description:
2 failures in scheduling/predicates.go:1247 — 'Did not find scheduled condition for pod pfpod'. The test creates a pod and waits for the PodScheduled condition to appear in pod status. Our apiserver stores the pod but never adds the PodScheduled condition.

In a real k8s cluster the scheduler sets this condition. In u7s the kube-scheduler binary runs externally and should be setting it via the pod status subresource. The failure likely means either:
1. The scheduler is not setting the condition (scheduler not running or not connecting)
2. The pod status subresource update is being dropped

Note: the pod JSON seen in the log (builder.go:157) shows conditions include PodReadyToStartContainers/Initialized/Ready/ContainersReady but NOT PodScheduled — suggesting the condition is not being set at any point. The $setElementOrder in the status hints this came from a strategic-merge-patch, which we don't support — so the kubelet status update may itself be failing.

Deferred until strategic-merge-patch (mayor-w5bt) is resolved, as that may be the actual root cause for the missing condition.
notes:
Unblocked: mayor-w5bt (strategic-merge-patch) closed in PR #279. PodScheduled condition can now be investigated.
PR #334: PodScheduled=False initialized on create, set to True in bind_pod; 5 regression tests.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #334 (merged): PodScheduled=False initialized on create; set to True in bind_pod.

title: fix(events): preserve EventSeries and CreationTimestamp on Event PATCH/update
description:
1 failure: core_events.go:144 — after patching an Event to set Series.Count=100 and Series.LastObservedTime, the returned Event has Series=nil and CreationTimestamp={} (zero value) instead of the patched values.

Diff from log:
  - CreationTimestamp: s"2026-05-27 02:24:57 +0000 UTC"
  + CreationTimestamp: v1.Time{}
  - Series: s"&EventSeries{Count:100,LastObservedTime:2017-09-19 13:49:16 +0000 UTC,}"
  + Series: nil

Root cause: the Event PATCH handler (or the JSON serialization round-trip) is dropping the 'series' field and zeroing 'creationTimestamp'. This is likely a missing field in the Event JSON schema stored in the DB — 'series' is an optional nested object (EventSeries with count+lastObservedTime) that may not be in our Object storage path. The creationTimestamp zero is a separate issue: our store may be normalizing empty timestamps.

Source: k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e/instrumentation/core_events.go:144
close_reason: PR #280 opened: fix(events): preserve EventSeries and creationTimestamp through PATCH

title: fix(list): populate continue token in chunked list responses
description:
2 conformance failures in chunking.go: the apiserver does return a continue token for the first page (chunking.go:98 shows 'Retrieved 17/17 results with rv 5925 and continue L3Jl...') but the test fails at chunking.go:108 asserting the continue field is not nil. This suggests the continue token is present in the response but not being decoded/populated into the ListMeta.Continue field that the client reads.

Possible causes:
1. The continue token is set in the response JSON but the field name or encoding is wrong, so the k8s client fails to deserialize it.
2. The second-page request (using the continue token) returns all results instead of a partial page, and the final page has a nil continue — but the test expects the last page to have nil, not an intermediate page.

chunking.go:108 assertion: 'Expected <*int64 | 0x0>: nil not to be nil' — this looks like it's asserting on RemainingItemCount, not the continue token itself.

Investigate: read chunking.go:83-120 in the k8s source to understand exactly what the test asserts. The apiserver list handler may need to populate metadata.remainingItemCount in chunked responses.

Source: k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e/apimachinery/chunking.go:108, :160
close_reason: PR #279 opened

title: fix(discovery): add flowcontrol.apiserver.k8s.io/v1 to API group discovery
description:
2 conformance failures: flowcontrol.go:290 and flowcontrol.go:536 both fail with 'expected flowcontrol API group/version, got [...]' — the API groups list returned by /apis does not include flowcontrol.apiserver.k8s.io. The test checks that the group exists in discovery before doing anything else, so it fails immediately.

Fix: register flowcontrol.apiserver.k8s.io/v1 in the discovery endpoint. The resources under this group (FlowSchema, PriorityLevelConfiguration) don't need to be functional — they just need to be listed in /apis and /apis/flowcontrol.apiserver.k8s.io/v1. A stub that returns empty lists is sufficient to unblock these 2 tests.

Source: k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e/apimachinery/flowcontrol.go:290, :536
close_reason: PR #278 opened — flowcontrol.apiserver.k8s.io/v1 registered in discovery

title: infra: worker-isolated apiserver test environment
description:
Workers currently cannot run live HTTP integration tests (kubectl create, sonobuoy) without conflicting with the shared host apiserver and VM kubelet. Need an isolation strategy before dispatching workers that require runtime validation.

Options under evaluation by operator:
1. Port-isolated host stacks (u7s-apiserver on unique port + state-db, no kubelet, HTTP-level validation only)
2. Ephemeral Lima VMs per worker (full isolation, heavy: 5-10 min startup, ~2GB RAM each)
3. Hybrid: cargo tests in workers, mayor holds the single sonobuoy slot
4. kubernetes-in-docker (requires containerizing u7s, significant infra lift)

Blocked on operator decision. Do not dispatch until decided.
notes: Resolved: per-VM WORKDIR isolation (temp/u7s-<name>/) + loopback IP aliasing (U7S_HOST_IP) landed in #464/#465/#469/#471. Workers invoke run-all.sh with U7S_VM_NAME=lima-node-<name> for a fully isolated stack. Up to 6 VMs available in parallel (soft limit: memory). No new infra needed.
close_reason: Closed

title: feat(patch): support application/strategic-merge-patch+json on namespace and core resources
description:
4 conformance failures from PATCH requests with Content-Type: application/strategic-merge-patch+json. Currently the apiserver returns 415 UnsupportedMediaType. The e2e webhook tests label namespaces using strategic merge patch.

Observed failure: 'error labeling namespace webhook-7006: unsupported media type application/strategic-merge-patch+json; use application/merge-patch+json'
File: test/e2e/apimachinery/webhook.go:2415

For many core types (Namespace, Pod, etc.), strategic-merge-patch degenerates to merge-patch behaviour — the strategic merge directives (replace/merge list keys) are only relevant for arrays, and most label/annotation patches don't use arrays. A pragmatic approach: accept strategic-merge-patch and apply it as merge-patch (RFC 7386) for now. This closes the conformance gap without requiring a full strategic merge implementation.

Deferred from prior sessions as complexity was unclear. Now confirmed as 4 distinct test failures.
close_reason: PR #279 opened

title: Add kubelet-reconnect script for iterate-on-apiserver workflow
description:
When iterating on the apiserver (cargo build --release && scripts/u7s-start.sh --reset), the developer needs to reconnect the kubelet to the new apiserver CA without re-provisioning the VM. Currently this requires running scripts/conformance/lima-start.sh which is long, mixes first-time provisioning with reconnect, and is not obviously safe to re-run.

Fix:
1. Add scripts/kubelet-reconnect.sh — does ONLY: copy kubeconfig (rewritten for host.lima.internal), copy CA cert, write kubelet drop-in, systemctl daemon-reload + restart kubelet, wait for node to appear. No VM provisioning, no iptables, no sonobuoy. ~30 lines.

2. Update the 'next steps' block in scripts/u7s-start.sh to print two clear paths:
   - First run (VM not yet provisioned): scripts/conformance/lima-start.sh
   - Subsequent runs (VM exists): scripts/kubelet-reconnect.sh

3. Add a comment at the top of scripts/conformance/lima-start.sh: 'For day-to-day iteration after initial provisioning, use scripts/kubelet-reconnect.sh instead.'

Files to modify: scripts/u7s-start.sh, scripts/conformance/lima-start.sh
Files to create: scripts/kubelet-reconnect.sh

The iptables DNAT rule (10.96.0.1 → host.lima.internal) survives VM restarts only if the VM was stopped cleanly; on a running VM it persists in memory. kubelet-reconnect.sh should re-apply it idempotently (same as lima-start.sh already does: delete+add).
close_reason: Fixed in PR #274 — scripts/kubelet-reconnect.sh added

title: Remove #[allow(dead_code)] suppressions — delete or use the dead code
description:
Three dead_code suppressions need real fixes (not allow hacks):

1. crates/apiserver/src/rbac.rs:44 — AggregationRule struct and ClusterRole.aggregation_rule field are marked dead_code. controller-manager/src/lib.rs has its own copy. Either wire aggregation_rule into the apiserver RBAC evaluator (correct fix: aggregate ClusterRoles before policy eval) or delete the struct and field from rbac.rs since the apiserver never uses it.

2. crates/apiserver/src/types.rs:222 — ResourceMeta.namespaced field is set on construction but never read at runtime (routing is done at the axum router level). Either use it (e.g. assert at registration time that cluster-scoped resources are not registered under namespaced routes) or delete the field entirely.

3. crates/apiserver/src/handlers/json_patch.rs:16 — PatchQueryParams.field_validation has #[allow(dead_code)] but the field IS constructed in tests (resource.rs:1905,1979) and parsed from the query string. The allow is wrong — check if removing it silences the warning without the allow (the field may not be dead at all, just not read after deserialization because it is intentionally ignored). If dead: document the ignore with a comment on the struct; if not dead: remove the allow.

Each fix must not regress existing tests. File follow-on beads for any new work discovered.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #276

title: Improve kubectl table columns for non-pod resources
description: crates/apiserver/src/handlers/table.rs build_table() routes to build_generic_table() for everything except pods, returning only Name+Age. Real kubectl -o wide shows resource-specific columns for all common types. Add typed table builders for at least: Nodes (STATUS, ROLES, AGE, VERSION, INTERNAL-IP, EXTERNAL-IP, OS-IMAGE, KERNEL-VERSION, CONTAINER-RUNTIME for wide), Deployments (READY, UP-TO-DATE, AVAILABLE, AGE), Services (TYPE, CLUSTER-IP, EXTERNAL-IP, PORT(S), AGE), ReplicaSets (DESIRED, CURRENT, READY, AGE), StatefulSets (READY, AGE), DaemonSets (DESIRED, CURRENT, READY, UP-TO-DATE, AVAILABLE, AGE), Namespaces (STATUS, AGE), ConfigMaps (DATA, AGE), Secrets (TYPE, DATA, AGE), ServiceAccounts (SECRETS, AGE). Pattern: add a branch in build_table() per (group, plural) pair, same pattern as the existing pod branch. Tests: assert column names and representative cell values for each new type. File: crates/apiserver/src/handlers/table.rs only.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #275

title: Add SubjectAccessReview protobuf decoder for kubelet webhook authorization
description: Kubelet sends SubjectAccessReview as protobuf to /apis/authorization.k8s.io/v1/subjectaccessreviews. No decoder exists; extract_body returns raw bytes to serde_json which fails with 'expected value at line 1 column 1'. Kubelet sees auth denial, returns InternalError to kubectl. Fix: add decode_subject_access_review_proto in crates/apiserver/src/proto.rs, register in decode_core_proto_by_kind. Also add TokenReview decoder (same issue for authentication webhook). Tests: wire-level proto decode tests for both types. Ref: .claude/plans/the-real-fix-here-peppy-thimble.md
close_reason: Fixed in PR #272 — SubjectAccessReview and TokenReview protobuf decoders merged to main (f0dbc02)

title: batch/v1 proto body decoding: CronJob POST returns 400 from e2e pod
description:
The e2e CronJob conformance test fails because the Go client sends CronJob objects as Content-Type: application/vnd.kubernetes.protobuf. Our extract_body() only decodes core/v1 proto types. batch/v1 types (CronJob, Job) have no decoder and the raw proto bytes are returned to Object::from_bytes() which fails with 'invalid JSON: expected value at line 1 column 1'. This is a per-test failure (not a panic), but it will cause many conformance tests to fail once the chunking panic is fixed.

Possible fix approaches:
A) Add batch/v1 proto decoders (CronJob, Job) using prost with batch API proto definitions
B) Return 415 Unsupported Media Type with Accept-Post: application/json when we can't decode a proto body, so clients retry with JSON (most correct but requires client cooperation)
C) Teach the fallback to accept content-type:application/json in the sub-envelope even when outer is proto
close_reason: Fixed in PR #271 — batch/v1 CronJob and Job protobuf decoders merged to main (109a6b4)

title: feat(apiserver): implement discovery.k8s.io/v1 EndpointSlices API
description: KCM hammers the apiserver every ~45s: 'failed to list *v1.EndpointSlice: Resource discovery.k8s.io/v1/endpointslices not found'. This floods kcm.log and causes KCM backoff loops. Implement the EndpointSlice collection (discovery.k8s.io/v1) — at minimum stub it as an empty list so KCM stops retrying. Relevant: endpointslice-controller is in the --controllers list in 04-start-kcm.sh.
close_reason: merged PR #269 — discovery.k8s.io/v1 EndpointSlices implemented

title: TokenRequest response missing ExpirationSeconds — kubelet token_manager falls back on every SA token
description: kubelet logs show 'Expiration seconds was nil for token request' for every pod throughout conformance run. Our SA token endpoint (POST /api/v1/namespaces/{ns}/serviceaccounts/{name}/token) returns a TokenRequestStatus without ExpirationTimestamp or ExpirationSeconds populated correctly. Kubelet uses a fallback but this is a conformance gap and will cause test failures on SA token-dependent tests.
close_reason: merged PR #265 — spec.expirationSeconds populated in TokenRequest response

title: pod spec.dnsPolicy not persisted/returned — kubelet falls back to ClusterFirst on every pod
description: kubelet logs show 'Failed to get DNS type for pod. Falling back to DNSClusterFirst policy. err=invalid DNSPolicy=' for every pod (sonobuoy, e2e-job, coredns) throughout conformance run. Our store is returning spec.dnsPolicy as empty string instead of the value set at creation time (e.g. ClusterFirst). Affects all pods. Conformance gap — pod DNS config is a testable surface.
close_reason: merged PR #264 — spec.dnsPolicy preserved on pod round-trip

title: sonobuoy retrieve: capture results tarball before aggregator pod exits
description: sonobuoy run-all.sh completes but sonobuoy retrieve gets EOF because the aggregator pod has already exited by the time retrieve runs. The tarball exists (sonobuoy status --json shows tar-info) but the HTTP endpoint on the pod is gone. Fix: in 06-run-sonobuoy.sh (or run-all.sh), run 'sonobuoy retrieve' immediately after '--wait' returns, before any cleanup. Alternative: copy the tarball out of the pod volume before the pod terminates (kubectl cp sonobuoy/sonobuoy:/tmp/sonobuoy /local/path). The duplicate-aggregator-pod warning is also a symptom: --reset must fully drain the sonobuoy namespace (wait for Terminating→gone) before starting a new run, otherwise the old aggregator pod is still visible when sonobuoy create runs.
close_reason: sonobuoy retrieve timing fixed in PR #257: added drain loop after sonobuoy delete --wait to ensure old aggregator pod is fully gone before next run; retrieve ordering was already correct

title: Collection DELETE on pods returns 405
description: sonobuoy cleanup calls DELETE /api/v1/namespaces/sonobuoy/pods?labelSelector=sonobuoy-run=<id> (collection delete with labelSelector). Server returns 405 'does not allow this method on the requested resource'. Need to handle DELETE on resource collections, filtering by labelSelector and deleting all matching objects.

close_reason: Node /proxy/ subresource implemented in proxy.rs, route registered in main.rs. PR #252 merged.

title: kubectl get pods -o wide shows only NAME+AGE columns
description: kubectl get pods -o wide (and plain get pods) only shows NAME and AGE, missing STATUS, READY, RESTARTS, IP, NODE columns. These come from the server-side table response (application/json;as=Table). The apiserver's table encoding for pods is likely not populating column definitions.

title: SelfSubjectAccessReview POST returns 415 UnsupportedMediaType
description: POST to /apis/authorization.k8s.io/v1/selfsubjectaccessreviews returns 415 UnsupportedMediaType with message 'Expected request with Content-Type: application/json'. kubectl auth can-i uses this endpoint. The SelfSubjectAccessReview handler likely has a different content-type requirement or body extraction path than regular resource handlers. Reproduce: kubectl auth can-i create pods -n default
close_reason: SelfSubjectAccessReview 415 fix landed in PR #253

title: kubectl logs fails: apiserver cannot proxy kubelet log requests (401 Unauthorized)
description: kubectl logs <pod> fails with 'kubelet request failed: error sending request for url (https://<node-ip>:10250/containerLogs/...)'. The apiserver proxies log requests to kubelet at port 10250. Kubelet responds 401 Unauthorized because the apiserver is not presenting a valid client certificate that kubelet trusts for log access. In real kube-apiserver, log proxying uses the apiserver's kubelet client cert (a separate cert signed by the cluster CA that kubelet accepts). u7s does not have a kubelet client cert configuration — it either does not present a cert, or presents one kubelet does not trust. This blocks: kubectl logs, kubectl exec, kubectl port-forward (all go through the same proxy path). Lower priority than fieldValidation bug since sonobuoy conformance tests do not require kubectl logs to pass.

title: CIDR-based clusterIP auto-allocation for Services
description:
When a Service is created without spec.clusterIP (or with spec.clusterIP=""), the apiserver should auto-allocate an IP from a configured CIDR range (--service-cluster-ip-range, e.g. 10.96.0.0/12). Currently u7s stores whatever the caller provides with no allocation.

Design: use the existing SQLite store's CAS uniqueness guarantee rather than a new table or in-memory bitmap.

Allocation protocol:
1. Parse the CIDR range at startup; iterate candidate IPs (skip network address, skip first IP reserved for kubernetes/default svc, skip broadcast).
2. To claim IP X: attempt store.put_sync('/registry/service-ips/X', sentinel, create_only=true). The objects table has UNIQUE on key — if another writer claimed X concurrently, the CAS fails. Retry with next candidate.
3. On Service DELETE: store.delete('/registry/service-ips/<clusterIP>') to release.
4. On startup: scan /registry/service-ips/* to reconstruct in-memory 'known allocated' set for fast iteration (avoid always starting from .1).

std::net::Ipv4Addr arithmetic suffices for iteration — no external CIDR crate needed. u32::from(Ipv4Addr) + 1 walks the range.

Config: add --service-cluster-ip-range flag (default 10.96.0.0/12 matching kubeadm) to main.rs. Pass into AppState.

Scope: crates/apiserver/src/main.rs (flag), crates/apiserver/src/state.rs (allocator field), crates/apiserver/src/handlers/defaults.rs (wire into apply_defaults for Services on create). The apply_defaults function already runs at every write path.

Note: headless services (clusterIP='None') skip allocation. ExternalName services skip allocation. Only ClusterIP-type services need it.
close_reason: Merged as PR #243 (6cf619f). CIDR-based clusterIP auto-allocation via CAS on /registry/service-ips/ sentinels. --service-cluster-ip-range flag, ServiceIpAllocator in state.rs, maybe_allocate_cluster_ip in create path, release on DELETE. 6 new unit tests.
